## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_oscillatory2d_compiled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native general-phase2D oscillatory cubature; owned phase program references match physical coordinates and omega has inverse phase dimension. Evaluation limit applies separately to each compiled program.

General-phase fallback for `integral f(x, y) exp(i omega phi(x, y)) dx dy`
over the box `[lo, hi]`.

[`filon2d`] is moment-corrected only for a linear phase. For a nonlinear
phase this fallback integrates the real and imaginary oscillating
integrands directly with [`cubature_genz_malik`]: deterministic and
reliable while the adaptive partition resolves the oscillation, but its
cost grows with `|omega|` (there is no frequency-independent 2-D Levin
collocation). The tolerance is used as both absolute and relative
tolerance of the two cubatures, with an integrand budget of
`OSC2D_MAX_EVALS` evaluations per component.

A non-finite phase at the box corners, edge midpoints or centre, or any
other invalid argument, returns `NaN` with `converged == false`.

Native advection_1d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

Solves `u_t + a u_x = 0` on the periodic domain `[x0, x1)` with `n` nodes
(`x1` is identified with `x0`). Stable for `|a| dt / dx <= 1`, checked
up front.

[`PdeError::Unstable`], [`PdeError::InvalidInput`] or
[`PdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_heat_1d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Float, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Native heat_1d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

Solves `u_t = alpha u_xx` on `grid` with Crank-Nicolson time stepping
(`steps` equal steps up to `t_end`); `bc = [left, right]`.

The scheme is second-order in space and time and unconditionally stable.

# Errors
[`PdeError::InvalidInput`] for a bad grid, step count or `alpha <= 0`;
[`PdeError::SolveFailed`] or [`PdeError::NonFinite`] otherwise.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_method_of_lines_1d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, String, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Native stiff1D method of lines. Compiled RHS inputs have domains(time,length,value,value/length,value/length^2),output value/time. Initial program is length->value. Method Radau5 or Bdf1..Bdf5; physical atol and all step bounds retain the grid time/value domains; explicit attempted-step and per-program evaluation budgets. field_data exposes native accepted steps/evaluations.

Method of lines for `u_t = F(t, x, u, u_x, u_xx)` on a 1D grid with a stiff ODE solver.

Semi-discretises with second-order central differences (ghost nodes for
Neumann ends, Dirichlet nodes held fixed) and integrates the ODE system to
`t_end`. Each boundary callback is evaluated once at `(endpoint, 0)` and
its spatial value is used throughout the solve.

# Errors
[`PdeError::InvalidInput`] for a bad grid or `t_end`, [`PdeError::Ode`] if
the integrator fails.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_method_of_lines_1d_timed` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Tensor<[2], String>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, String, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Stiff 1D method of lines with two time-dependent compiled boundary programs in left-to-right order. Set each kind to Dirichlet for a measured field value or Neumann for a measured outward derivative. Each boundary program takes a measured Time. The returned field retains physical samples and exact prescribed Dirichlet endpoint values at the requested final time.

Integrates a 1D method-of-lines problem with time-dependent endpoint data.

The endpoint callbacks receive each RHS evaluation time, including internal
integrator stages. Dirichlet endpoints are excluded from the ODE unknowns.
Neumann data are outward normal derivatives. The returned field includes
the prescribed Dirichlet values at `t_end`.

# Errors
Returns [`PdeError::InvalidInput`] for an invalid grid or final time,
[`PdeError::NonFinite`] for non-finite boundary data, or [`PdeError::Ode`]
when the integrator fails.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_poisson_2d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Float, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Native poisson_2d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

Solves `-(u_xx + u_yy) = f` with the 5-point stencil;
`bc = [left, right, bottom, top]`.

A problem with Neumann conditions on all four sides is singular and is
rejected with [`PdeError::Unsupported`], unless `solver` is
[`PoissonSolver::MeanFree`], which solves it in the zero-mean subspace when
the data are compatible.

# Errors
[`PdeError::InvalidInput`], [`PdeError::Unsupported`] (pure Neumann, or CG
with a Neumann side), [`PdeError::SolveFailed`] (singular matrix or CG
not converged), [`PdeError::Incompatible`] or [`PdeError::NotConverged`]
([`PoissonSolver::MeanFree`]).

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_wave_1d` (Experimental)

```aevia

```

Native wave_1d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_wave_2d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Float, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Native wave_2d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

Solves `u_tt = c^2 (u_xx + u_yy)` with leapfrog; stable for
`c dt sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2) <= 1`.

# Errors
As [`wave_1d`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_pde_wave_3d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/pde/grid/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Float, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/analysis/pde/field/v1
```

Native wave_3d in the grid physical reference frame. Boundary handles share that frame. Heat coefficient L^2/T,wave/advection L/T; primary compiled output V for initial data or V/L^2 for Poisson; secondary V/T only for wave. Method SparseLu/Cg/MeanFree for elliptic,Upwind/LaxWendroff for advection; relative>0. Dedicated Laplace ignores primary; other unused coefficients/secondary are explicit placeholder Values.

Solves `u_tt = c^2 (u_xx + u_yy + u_zz)` with leapfrog; stable for
`c dt sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2 + 1/dz^2) <= 1`.

# Errors
As [`wave_1d`](super::wave_1d).


Solves an ODE system forward in time using the Dormand-Prince 5(4) method.

The output includes the initial state and every accepted step. The
last time is exactly the requested endpoint when it is reached.
Invalid controls, non-finite rates, or a step that cannot advance
return the accepted prefix. Tolerances are nonnegative and at
least one must be positive.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_physics_explicit_euler` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/ode/rhs/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, String, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Evolves a native measured ODE tape using Forward, Midpoint or Heun with a signed time step. The last interval is shortened to reach the requested endpoint. Returns time and mixed physical state for each accepted grid point. Forward needs one tape evaluation per step and Midpoint and Heun need two.

Solves an ODE with a fixed Euler formula, ending exactly at the requested time.

The sign of `dt` must agree with the direction of travel. Times are located
on the nominal grid from the start, without accumulating rounding drift.
State updates use the represented interval between successive grid points.
The last step ends at `t_span.1`, shortening the interval if necessary.
A zero-length span returns the initial state without evaluating the RHS.

# Errors

Returns an error for invalid times, a zero or oppositely signed step,
mismatched dimensions, non-finite states or right-hand sides, unrepresentable
progress, or a history whose size cannot be represented or reserved.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_physics_rk4` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/ode/rhs/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Float, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native generic ODE solver instantiated on an immutable tape implementing the real OdeSystem trait. Independent physical state/time references, normalized rtol/atol and a shared explicit oracle budget are preserved; incomplete native paths are errors.

Solves an ODE system using the classic 4th-order Runge-Kutta method with a fixed step size.

This method is a widely used, robust, and relatively accurate explicit method for
approximating the solutions of ordinary differential equations.

# Arguments
* `system` - The ODE system to solve, implementing the `OdeSystem` trait.
* `y0` - The initial state vector.
* `t_span` - A tuple `(t_start, t_end)` specifying the time interval.
* `dt` - The fixed time step.

# Returns
A `Vec` of tuples `(time, state_vector)` representing the solution at each time step.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_physics_rosenbrock_solve` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/ode/rhs/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Int) -> None | Some(Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>)
```

Actual native generic ODE solver instantiated on an immutable tape implementing the real OdeSystem trait. Independent physical state/time references, normalized rtol/atol and a shared explicit oracle budget are preserved; incomplete native paths are errors.

Integrates `y' = f(t, y)` from `t0` to `t1` with the adaptive Rosenbrock
method ROS2 (L-stable, order 2; `γ = 1 + 1/√2`), the error estimated
against the linearly implicit Euler step.

Returns the accepted `(t, y)` pairs, or `None` when a linear system is
singular or the step size underflows.

Solves a 2D orbital mechanics problem using the energy-conserving semi-implicit Euler method.

This scenario simulates the orbit of a celestial body around a much more massive star,

stable, realistic orbits over long simulation times.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_qp_active_set_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Float[_]) -> None | Some({ d: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, lambda: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, mu: Tensor<1, Float[_]> })
```

Native active-set QP with positive coordinate,objective,equality and inequality references. H has E/D^2,g E/D,Aeq C/D,beq C,Aineq G/D,bineq G; result step D and multipliers E/C,E/G.

Solves `min 0.5 d^T H d + c^T d` subject to `A_eq d = b_eq` and
`A_ineq d <= b_ineq` by a primal active-set method started from `d = 0`,
which must be feasible (`b_ineq >= 0`).

The KKT system of the working set is solved exactly at every step, so
the returned multipliers are those of the Lagrangian
`0.5 d^T H d + c^T d + lambda . (A_eq d - b_eq) + mu . (A_ineq d - b_ineq)`.
Returns `None` if a KKT system stays singular after regularisation or
the working set fails to settle within the iteration budget.

## `numerical_callback.num_analysis_quadrature_gk_breakpoints_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float) -> Float) -> { value: Float[_], error: None | Some(Float[_]), evaluations: Int, converged: None | Some(Bool) }
```

Integrates a normalized callback with a shared tolerance and panel budget across known interior breakpoints. The Float parameters are `[a, b, abs_tol, rel_tol, ...breakpoints]` and the integer controls are `[rule, max_panels]` with rule 0 for G7K15 or 1 for G10K21. Pass positive coordinate and integrand reference scales and a callback evaluation budget. The result value and error have the product of the two reference dimensions.

Adaptive Gauss–Kronrod integration split at known interior breakpoints.

Supply breakpoints in increasing coordinate order even for reversed limits.
Kronrod samples each subinterval's interior, avoiding the breakpoints for
ordinary representable intervals. The panel budget and the tolerance
`max(abs_tol, rel_tol * |value|)` apply to the entire partition. Exhausting
the refinement budget returns an estimate with `converged = false` if the
error is still above tolerance.

# Errors
Returns an error for invalid endpoints, tolerances or breakpoints, an
insufficient initial panel budget, a nonfinite estimate, or cancellation.

A root of `f` near `guess`, by Newton's method with a bisection fallback.

If no sign change is found, a local minimum of the residual magnitude can
identify a touching root. A callback that rounds residuals to zero limits
positional accuracy. Positive offsets below the local resolution can be
indistinguishable from a touching root.

root is found.


Native homotopy_univariate on normalized polynomial coefficients with a positive physical coordinate reference; returned complex roots restore its units. Degree and iteration work are bounded before native calls.

Homotopy continuation for the roots of a real-coefficient polynomial.

Homotopy continuation for a polynomial with real coefficients: tracks
the roots of `H(z, t) = (1-t) * gamma * (z^n - 1) + t * p(z)` from the
roots of unity at `t = 0` to those of `p` at `t = 1` with predictor
(Euler) and Newton corrector steps and adaptive step size.

This is the one-variable instance of total-degree homotopy
continuation; the random complex `gamma` is fixed (deterministic) so
generic paths do not cross.

# Errors
[`RootError::Invalid`] for constant polynomials,
[`RootError::NoConvergence`] if a path fails to be tracked.


All complex roots of a complex polynomial by Jenkins-Traub.

All complex roots of a polynomial with complex coefficients
(`(re, im)` pairs, ascending order) by the three-stage Jenkins-Traub
algorithm (no-shift, fixed-shift and variable-shift stages with
shifts on a circle just inside the smallest root modulus), polished
by Newton iteration against the original polynomial.

Roots are found in order of increasing modulus and deflated forward,
which is the numerically stable direction. Roots at zero are
detected from vanishing low-order coefficients.

# Errors
[`RootError::Invalid`] for constant polynomials,
[`RootError::NoConvergence`] if the shift iteration fails.


Actual native sde_adaptive_noncommutative_stratonovich_with with independently scaled physical state, normalized rtol/atol, seed, max_steps, and explicit evaluation budget. Noncommutative variants require bounded cells/terms and retain genuine conditional Levy areas.

Adaptive-step integration of a **Stratonovich** SDE with **non-commutative**
noise on `[t0, t1]`, by exact conversion to Ito form.

As [`sde_adaptive_stratonovich_with`], with the controller of
[`sde_adaptive_noncommutative_with`] (fine cell grid, Chen's relation); the
returned path is the controlled Ito-Milstein solution of the equivalent Ito
SDE, which converges to the Stratonovich solution. The Brownian path is the

# Errors
As [`sde_adaptive_noncommutative_with`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_adaptive_noncommutative_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> rssn/native/analysis/sde/path/v1
```

Actual native sde_adaptive_noncommutative_with with independently scaled physical state, normalized rtol/atol, seed, max_steps, and explicit evaluation budget. Noncommutative variants require bounded cells/terms and retain genuine conditional Levy areas.

Adaptive-step Milstein integration of an Ito SDE with **non-commutative**
noise on `[t0, t1]`.

The Brownian path is fixed in advance on a grid of `opts.cells` cells, each
with its increment and its Levy areas ([`levy_areas`]); a step is a union of
cells, whose increment and areas are combined *exactly* by Chen's relation
`A_{0,2h} = A_1 + A_2 + (W_1 x W_2 - W_2 x W_1) / 2`. Splitting a rejected
step is therefore merging fewer of the same cells: the realised path is the
same for every step sequence, the errors of the controller cannot bias the
noise, and a fixed-step reference on the cells sees exactly the path the
adaptive solver used ([`noncommutative_noise_grid`]).

The error control is that of [`sde_adaptive_with`], with the Milstein
correction built from the areas (for commutative noise the correction is the
same function of the increments, so the estimate and the controller agree
with it in law). A step of a single cell that is still rejected ends the run
with [`SdeError::StepLimit`]: use more cells.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`], [`SdeError::NonFinite`] or [`SdeError::StepLimit`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_adaptive_stratonovich_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> rssn/native/analysis/sde/path/v1
```

Actual native sde_adaptive_stratonovich_with with independently scaled physical state, normalized rtol/atol, seed, max_steps, and explicit evaluation budget. Noncommutative variants require bounded cells/terms and retain genuine conditional Levy areas.

Adaptive-step integration of a **Stratonovich** SDE `dX = a dt + g o dW` with
commutative noise on `[t0, t1]`, by exact conversion to Ito form.

The drift is replaced by the Ito-equivalent drift
([`stratonovich_to_ito_drift`]) and [`sde_adaptive_with`] runs on the Ito SDE
`dX = a~ dt + g dW`, which has the same solution process. The returned path is
therefore the *controlled Ito-Milstein solution of the equivalent Ito SDE*; it
converges to the Stratonovich solution of the original coefficients (for
`dX = sigma X o dW` to `X_0 exp(sigma W_T)`), with the error control of
[`sde_adaptive_with`] applied to the converted drift. The conversion uses
finite-difference derivatives of `g`, which costs `2m + 1` extra diffusion
evaluations per drift evaluation.

# Errors
As [`sde_adaptive_with`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_adaptive_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> rssn/native/analysis/sde/path/v1
```

Actual native sde_adaptive_with with independently scaled physical state, normalized rtol/atol, seed, max_steps, and explicit evaluation budget. Noncommutative variants require bounded cells/terms and retain genuine conditional Levy areas.

Adaptive-step integration of an Ito SDE with commutative noise on
`[t0, t1]`.

Each step computes the Euler-Maruyama and the Milstein update from the
same Brownian increment; the Milstein correction plus the trapezoidal
drift correction `h |a(y_EM) - a(y)| / 2` estimate the local error of
the former (so additive noise and strongly varying drifts both control
the step). A step is accepted when the scaled error
`max_i |delta_i| / (atol + rtol |y_i|)` is at most one (the tolerance
bounds the local, not the global, pathwise error; the global error
accumulates like a random walk). Rejected increments are split by
Brownian bridges and re-used, so the realised path is a genuine
Brownian sample independent of the step sequence. The returned solution
is the Milstein one.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`], [`SdeError::NonFinite`] or [`SdeError::StepLimit`].


Actual native Chen aggregation retains the same physical Brownian path and iterated integrals.

Merges groups of `group` consecutive steps.

The increments add up and the iterated integrals combine exactly as
`I_jl = sum_k I_jl^k + sum_{k<k'} dW_j^k dW_l^{k'}`. Used to compare a
coarse scheme with a fine reference on the same Brownian path.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_levy_areas` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/rng/v1, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native conditional Levy areas. Supplied increments have sqrt(time) units and output flattened m by m Ito integrals have time units.

Samples the iterated Ito integrals `I_jl` of one step of length `h`.

The integrals are drawn conditionally on the increments `dw` by the Fourier expansion of the
Brownian bridge (Kloeden, Platen and Wright) with the Gaussian
approximation of the truncated tail that reproduces its full conditional
covariance (Wiktorsson's improvement): with `xi = dw / sqrt(h)`,

`I_jl / h = xi_j xi_l / 2 + A_jl + sqrt(rho) (mu_j xi_l - mu_l xi_j) + sqrt(rho) nu_jl`

for `j < l`, where `A` is the Fourier sum over `terms` modes, `rho` the
tail sum divided by `2 pi^2`, and `mu`, `nu` standard normal. The
remainder error decays like `1 / terms^{3/2}` in distribution; a few
terms suffice for strong order one.

`dw` contains the `m` supplied increments. The returned matrix is flat
and row-major. Pair evaluation can run in parallel, with the same RNG
draws and floating-point summation order for every worker count.

The correction uses the sampled iterated integrals of `noise` instead of the
symmetric products `(dW_j dW_k - delta_jk h) / 2`. For commutative noise it
is equivalent to [`milstein`] in law.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_milstein_noncommutative_stratonovich` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/sde/noise/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native milstein_noncommutative_stratonovich over one retained physical Brownian sample. The caller explicitly selects Ito/Stratonovich and commutative/noncommutative methods; no scheme substitution. Independent state dimensions and a shared native evaluation budget are preserved.

Milstein scheme (strong order 1) for **non-commutative** noise in the
*Stratonovich* interpretation `dX = a dt + g o dW`.

The correction is `sum_{j,l} (D_j g)_{.l} J_jl` with the Stratonovich iterated
integrals `J_jl = I_jl + delta_jl h / 2 = dW_j dW_l / 2 + A_jl` (`A` the Levy
area), i.e. the same sampled areas as [`milstein_noncommutative`] with the
diagonal shifted by `h / 2`. The drift is the Stratonovich drift, unchanged.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_milstein_stratonovich` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/sde/noise/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native milstein_stratonovich over one retained physical Brownian sample. The caller explicitly selects Ito/Stratonovich and commutative/noncommutative methods; no scheme substitution. Independent state dimensions and a shared native evaluation budget are preserved.

Milstein scheme (strong order 1) for the *Stratonovich* interpretation
`dX = a dt + g o dW` of the same coefficients; arguments as in
[`euler_maruyama`].

It differs from the Ito [`milstein`] only in the iterated integral of the
correction, `I_jk = dW_j dW_k / 2` instead of
`(dW_j dW_k - delta_jk h) / 2`: for scalar noise the correction is
`g g' dW^2 / 2` rather than `g g' (dW^2 - h) / 2`, so the two differ by the
Ito-Stratonovich drift correction `g g' h / 2` and converge to different
solutions. For `dX = sigma X dW` they are `X_0 exp(sigma W_T)` (here) and
`X_0 exp(sigma W_T - sigma^2 T / 2)` ([`milstein`]).

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_srk_noncommutative` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/sde/noise/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native srk_noncommutative over one retained physical Brownian sample. The caller explicitly selects Ito/Stratonovich and commutative/noncommutative methods; no scheme substitution. Independent state dimensions and a shared native evaluation budget are preserved.

Derivative-free stochastic Runge-Kutta scheme of strong order 1 for
**non-commutative** Ito noise (Kloeden-Platen, eq. 11.1.7).

With the supporting values `U^j = Y + a h + g^j sqrt(h)` (`g^j` the `j`-th
column of `g`, one per noise channel),

`Y' = Y + a h + sum_j g^j dW_j + h^{-1/2} sum_{j,l} (g^l(U^j) - g^l(Y)) I_jl`,

where `I_jl` are the sampled iterated Ito integrals of `noise`
([`sample_noise`]). It needs `m` extra diffusion evaluations per step and no
derivative of `g`. On commutative noise the Levy-area part cancels and it
agrees with [`srk_platen`] up to the `O(h)` of the supporting values.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_srk_noncommutative_stratonovich` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/sde/noise/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native srk_noncommutative_stratonovich over one retained physical Brownian sample. The caller explicitly selects Ito/Stratonovich and commutative/noncommutative methods; no scheme substitution. Independent state dimensions and a shared native evaluation budget are preserved.

The Stratonovich counterpart of [`srk_noncommutative`].

After Kloeden-Platen, eq. 11.1.10: with the Stratonovich iterated integrals
`J_jl = I_jl + delta_jl h / 2` and the Stratonovich drift it converges to the
solution of `dX = a dt + g o dW` with strong order 1.

Because `J_jj` has mean `h / 2` (unlike `I_jj`), the difference quotient must
be accurate to `O(h)`: the scheme uses the *central* supporting values
`U^j_{+-} = Y +- g^j sqrt(h)` and
`Y' = Y + a h + sum_j g^j dW_j + (2 sqrt(h))^{-1} sum_{j,l} (g^l(U^j_+) - g^l(U^j_-)) J_jl`
(a forward quotient would leave a systematic `O(sqrt(h))` error and only
strong order 1/2). It costs `2m` extra diffusion evaluations per step.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_srk_platen` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/sde/noise/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>
```

Actual native srk_platen over one retained physical Brownian sample. The caller explicitly selects Ito/Stratonovich and commutative/noncommutative methods; no scheme substitution. Independent state dimensions and a shared native evaluation budget are preserved.

Platen's derivative-free stochastic Runge-Kutta scheme for commutative
Itô noise, with strong order 1.

Each supplied Brownian increment has `m` components. The scheme replaces
the Milstein term with differences of the diffusion at supporting values
`x + a h + g_j sqrt(abs(h))`.
Corrections at extreme scales retain an out-of-range intermediate product
in scaled form when the weighted result is representable. An empty
increment sequence returns just `y0` without evaluating either callback.

# Errors
[`SdeError::Invalid`] or [`SdeError::NonFinite`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_sde_stratonovich_to_ito_drift` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1) -> rssn/native/analysis/sde/ito-drift/v1
```

Owned native Stratonovich-to-Ito drift recipe. Evaluation calls the actual native derivative-based conversion over the immutable physical reference frame, retaining no source callback lifetime.

The Ito-equivalent drift of a Stratonovich SDE `dX = a dt + g o dW`:
`a~_i = a_i + (1/2) sum_j sum_k g_{kj} d_k g_{ij}`.

The correction is `(1/2) sum_j (D_j g)_{.j}` with the directional derivative of
column `j` along itself, with the same scaled probes as the Milstein term.
The ordinary step is `eps = 1e-6 max(1, |y|_inf) / |g^j|`. A probe uses one
side at the floating-point range boundary when only that side is finite. The closure writes
`a~` into its output, so any Ito integrator applied to `(a~, g)` converges to
the Stratonovich solution of `(a, g)`.

Evaluates the cubic Hermite continuous extension at `t`.

Within an accepted step `[t_n, t_{n+1}]` the interpolant is the cubic
Hermite polynomial matching `y_n`, `y_{n+1}` and the endpoint slopes
`f(t_n, y_n)`, `f(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1})`. Returns `None` outside the
integrated range or when no step was accepted.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_series_sum_terms` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Estimates an infinite sum from a finite measured prefix, stopping at the requested absolute tolerance, the end of the prefix, or the term budget. The record's value and heuristic error have the term dimension. Missing estimates are None, and terms reports the number consumed.

Estimates an infinite sum from terms supplied in order.

This accepts an unbounded generator or a finite prefix. At each doubling
checkpoint it compares Wynn's epsilon algorithm on the most recent partial
sums, Richardson extrapolation on the doubling checkpoints, and the
Levin `u` transform of the first terms. A final partial block may still
contribute Wynn or Levin estimates. The calculation stops on the requested
tolerance, input exhaustion, or after evaluating `max_terms` terms.

The reported error is a change between estimates and is heuristic. When
extrapolation has insufficient data, the result is the available partial
sum with infinite error. A non-finite term or partial sum yields `NaN`
and infinite error, counting the triggering term in `terms`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_signal_fft` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Complex[_]>
```

Native signal fft; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Computes the one-dimensional discrete Fourier Transform.

This function uses the `rustfft` library to perform the FFT.

# Arguments
* `input` - A slice of complex samples. Its contents are preserved.

# Returns
A vector of complex numbers representing the FFT of the input.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::signal::fft;
use rustfft::num_complex::Complex;

let mut input = vec![
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
];

let output = fft(&mut input);

assert!((output[0].re - 4.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_signal_ifft` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Complex[_]>
```

Native signal ifft; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Computes the one-dimensional inverse discrete Fourier Transform.

This is the positive-sign transform followed by the `1/n`
normalisation, so `ifft(fft(x)) == x` (up to round-off) for every length.

# Arguments
* `input` - A mutable slice of complex frequency-domain samples.

# Returns
A vector of complex numbers representing the inverse transform.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::signal::fft;
use rssn::kernels::signal::ifft;
use rustfft::num_complex::Complex;

let mut input = vec![Complex::new(1.0, 0.5), Complex::new(-2.0, 0.0)];

let spectrum = fft(&mut input);

let back = ifft(&mut spectrum.clone());

assert!((back[0] - input[0]).norm() < 1e-12);
```


Short-time Fourier transform of complete frames with starts `hop` samples apart.

Returns full unnormalised complex spectra. The number of bins per frame is
the window length. Incomplete trailing frames are discarded. Empty windows,
zero hops and signals shorter than a window yield an empty result.

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_]) -> { status: String, x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, value: None | Some(Float[_]), iterations: None | Some(Int), bland_pivots: None | Some(Int) }
```

Native simplex LP with normalized coefficient conversion using positive coordinate/objective/constraint references; preserves Optimal,Infeasible,Unbounded without fabricated coordinates or objective.

Two-phase simplex: minimise `c . x` subject to rows `a_i . x (rel_i) b_i`
and `x >= 0`, with steepest-edge pricing and the Bland anti-cycling
fallback; see [`simplex_with`].

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_simplex_with_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, String>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, String, Float[_], Float[_], Float[_]) -> { status: String, x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, value: None | Some(Float[_]), iterations: None | Some(Int), bland_pivots: None | Some(Int) }
```

Native simplex LP with actual selectable Dantzig,SteepestEdge,Bland pricing and retained pivot statistics; independent positive coordinate/objective/constraint references.

Two-phase tableau simplex with a selectable pricing rule.

For [`Pricing::Dantzig`] and [`Pricing::SteepestEdge`] the solver
monitors degeneracy: after a run of consecutive pivots that do not
improve the objective it switches to Bland's rule (smallest-index
entering variable, ties in the ratio test broken by smallest basic
index) until a strictly improving pivot occurs, which guarantees
termination on cycling examples such as Beale's. The leaving-variable
tie-break is always Bland's.

Genuine native method with physical point and positive coordinate/output references. Callbacks operate normalized vectors; residual/gradient/Jacobian results restore their proper E,D units. Solver args x,xref,yref,normalized tolerance,iterations,budget,callback(s); numerical Jacobian args x,physical fx,xref,yref,budget,f; gradient args x,xref,yref,budget,f. Shared callback budget and original errors are preserved.

Solves the square nonlinear system `f(x) = 0` by Newton's method with a
finite-difference Jacobian.

## `numerical_callback.num_analysis_solve_root_bisection_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float) -> Float) -> { value: Float[_], error: None | Some(Float[_]), evaluations: Int, converged: None | Some(Bool) }
```

Normalized native solve::solve_root_bisection: parameters Float vector length3, exact nonnegative integer controls length1, positive coordinate reference D,positive value reference E,evaluation budget,then1 normalized Float callbacks. Results restore D*E for integrals,D for roots,E for sums. Error=None means native method supplies no finite error estimate; convergence flag retains native stopping status where available.

Finds a root of `f` in `interval` by bisection.

Endpoints may be in either order. A finite endpoint or midpoint whose
residual is zero or has magnitude less than `tolerance` is accepted.
Otherwise the absolute interval width is compared with the tolerance.
Zero tolerance disables approximate stopping. The two endpoint evaluations
are followed by at most `max_iter` midpoint evaluations. At the budget or
when no representable point remains inside the bracket, returns its midpoint.

# Errors
Returns an error for non-finite endpoints or function values, a negative
or non-finite tolerance, or endpoints with the same sign outside the tolerance.

Return the dimensionless complex solution to w exp(w) = z on integer branch k. When the imaginary component is signed zero on the negative real axis, its sign selects the side of the branch cut. The principal branch preserves small real and imaginary components near the origin.

The branch `k` of the Lambert W function: the solution of `w e^w = z`
in the strip of branch `k`.

On the negative real axis, a positive zero imaginary part selects the
upper lip and a negative zero selects the lower lip.

`W_0(0) = 0` and `W_k(0) = -∞` for `k != 0`; the branch point `-1/e`
gives `-1`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_special_complex_ln_gamma_complex` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Complex) -> Complex
```

Native special_complex ln_gamma_complex; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

The analytic branch of `ln Γ(z)`, defined and continuous on the plane cut
along the non-positive real axis, with `ln Γ(z + 1) = ln Γ(z) + ln z`.

Non-positive integers (the poles) give `+∞`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_stochastic_default_terms` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float) -> Int
```

Actual native stochastic method in explicit physical reference coordinates. Session/kind, storage, shape and evaluation limits are checked.

The default number of Fourier modes of the simulated Lévy areas for a step
(or Brownian cell) of size `h`: `clamp(ceil(1 / sqrt(h)), 16, 4096)`.

The truncation error of the area decays like `h p^(-3/2)` with the kernel's
Gaussian tail correction, so this rule keeps it far below the `O(h)` strong
error of the scheme at an `O(m^2 / sqrt(h))` sampling cost per step.


Actual native stochastic method in explicit physical reference coordinates. Session/kind, storage, shape and evaluation limits are checked.

Integrates one path per ensemble member, sequentially and order-preserving.

Member `i` uses [`ensemble_seed`] with `(seed, i)` as its own seed, so the result
does not depend on execution order or concurrency. The paths run one after
another because the Aevia interpreter closures are `!Send`; the kernel's
rayon ensemble would need a `Send + Sync` callback, which this build cannot
produce. The returned paths are in index order.

# Errors

The first member error, in index order.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_stochastic_events` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/stochastic/path/v1, Tensor<1, Dyn<term>>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native sign-change event detection on the native piecewise-linear stochastic path; this does not claim to detect unobserved between-node process crossings. Programs receive coherent physical time/state components.

Detects sign changes of `g_i(t, y)` along a path.

Between two consecutive nodes the path is the chord of [`Path::eval`]; a
crossing is a sign change of `g` at the two nodes in an allowed direction
(falling `g0 > 0 >= g1`, rising `g0 < 0 <= g1`, the kernel's convention
for ODE events), and its time is the root of `g` along the chord, found by
bisection. A node where `g` is exactly zero counts once (as the end of the
step that reaches it). Only the discretised path is watched: the
continuous process may cross and return between two nodes, which no
discrete scheme can see.

Hits come in time order. If an event is `terminal`, the returned path ends
at the first terminal hit (the hit is appended as its last node) and later
hits are dropped. The returned path is the input when nothing terminates.

Integrates `dX = a(t, X) dt + G(t, X) dW` from `y0`.

`drift` returns `n` values; `diffusion` returns `n` values for
[`Structure::Diagonal`] (the diagonal entries) or `n × m` values in
row-major order for [`Structure::General`].

Fixed/uniform-grid schedules use prescribed increments. Adaptive schedules
retain the requested method and use a bounded noise tree with coupled step
doubling, a separate drift-error check, and explicit resolution/work errors.
See the module documentation for tolerance scaling and finite allocations.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_stochastic_mlmc` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/sde/model/v1, rssn/native/analysis/stochastic/options/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native MLMC with coupled fine/coarse Brownian paths. Payoff compiled program receives physical state components; target RMSE and estimate/standard-error have payoff units and variance has their square. Explicit hierarchy/sample/work caps bound all native levels.

Estimate a terminal SDE expectation with multilevel Monte Carlo.

Estimates the expected value `E[payoff(X_{t1})]` of a terminal functional of an
SDE `dX = a(t, X) dt + G(t, X) dW` using Giles' Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC)
method with coupled fine/coarse Brownian paths (`\Delta W^{(c)}_k = \Delta W^{(f)}_{2k} + \Delta W^{(f)}_{2k+1}`)
and optimal sample allocation `N_l \propto \sqrt{V_l / C_l}`.

Each (level, sample index) draws from its own deterministic seeded stream.
A coupled fine/coarse pair shares that stream. The estimates for a given seed
may differ from versions that reused streams across levels.

# Errors

Returns [`SdeError`] if options or callback dimensions are invalid or if any
simulated trajectory becomes non-finite. Returns [`SdeError::StepLimit`] if cancelled
at a checkpoint between solves and payoff evaluations.

```aevia

```

Actual native stochastic method in explicit physical reference coordinates. Session/kind, storage, shape and evaluation limits are checked.

The state at time `t`, by linear interpolation between the accepted
nodes; `None` outside `[t_first, t_last]`.

A numerical SDE path is only known at its nodes. Between them the
interpolant is the chord, which is continuous and deterministic. It is
as accurate as the scheme itself (strong order at most 1, and a Brownian
path is only Hölder-1/2 between nodes anyway); it does not add the
within-step Brownian-bridge variance, so statistics of `eval` between
nodes understate the within-step variation by `O(dt)`. Use the node
values (`y`) when exact distributional statistics at the nodes are
wanted.

```aevia
(Int, Int, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native stochastic method in explicit physical reference coordinates. Session/kind, storage, shape and evaluation limits are checked.

Brownian increments for `steps` steps of `dt`, `m` components each, on the
language stream seeded with `seed`.

The argument order is the kernel's `sde_wiener(seed, m, steps, h)` so the
language surface, the manifest operator and this helper cannot drift:
`wiener(seed, m, steps, dt)[k][j]` is the increment of the `j`-th Wiener
process over `[t0 + k dt, t0 + (k+1) dt]`, drawn step-major (component order
inside a step), which is exactly the layout the kernel's fixed-step solvers
consume. A fixed-step integration with the same seed and structure therefore
consumes these numbers.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_free_flow_exact` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/symplectic/rigid-body/v1, Dyn<term>) -> Bool
```

Actual native geometric operation; physical rigid-body moments/torques use explicit positive SI M/L/T references, while orientations and composition coefficients are dimensionless.

**Exact** free rotation for time `t` of an asymmetric rigid body, in closed form.

With `d` the principal axis about which the polhode circulates, the body-frame angular
momentum is `L_d = +-A_d dn`, `L_p = A_p cn`, `L_s = A_s sn` (Jacobi functions of
`tau = tau_0 + omega t`, parameter `m`; Landau and Lifshitz, section 37). The orientation
follows from the Euler angles with the (space-fixed) angular momentum as polar axis:
`theta` and `psi` are algebraic in `L`, and the precession angle is
`phi(t) = |L| t / I_d + |L| (2T - L^2 / I_d) int_0^t dt' / (L^2 - L_d^2)`, an elliptic
integral of the **third kind** ([`crate::sim::elliptic::elliptic_pi`]). Symmetric tops and
steady rotations use the exact symmetric-top flow. Valid for any `t` (including negative).

Actual native geometric operation; physical rigid-body moments/torques use explicit positive SI M/L/T references, while orientations and composition coefficients are dimensionless.

Second-order symmetric step of the free rotor built on exact **symmetric-top flows**:
`exp(h/2 R_a) exp(h/2 R_b) exp(h S) exp(h/2 R_b) exp(h/2 R_a)` where `S` is the symmetric
top and `R_a`, `R_b` the single-axis remainders. Exact when the body is itself a symmetric
top and much more accurate than [`free_step`](Self::free_step) for nearly symmetric bodies.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_integrate_sampled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/mechanics/acceleration/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Int, Int) -> { steps: Tensor<1, Int>, states: Tensor<1, Dyn<term>> }
```

Integrates every step with a separable symplectic scheme. Retains step zero, each positive save_every multiple, and the final step. Each state preserves the physical positions followed by velocities. Step indices are exact and the signed step size uses the acceleration tape's time dimension.

Integrates a separable Hamiltonian and samples its phase state by step count.

Retains step zero, each multiple of `save_every`, and the final step.
`h` may be negative for backward integration. With zero `h` the sampled
state stays constant and the acceleration callback is skipped. Otherwise
`acc(q, a)` must write every element of `a` at each kick.

# Errors
Empty or unequal state slices, non-finite inputs, zero cadence, a
non-finite state or acceleration, an unavailable snapshot allocation,
or cancellation.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_ks_advance` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native physical-time KS advance with explicit positive gravitational parameter mu(L³/T²), bounded eta and a genuine tape perturbation acceleration. Callback budget failures and incomplete native endpoint errors are preserved.

Advances a perturbed two-body problem in KS variables for a given physical time.

The gravitational parameter is `mu`, the physical time `dt > 0` (RK4 in the fictitious time, step `ds = eta / omega` with the
harmonic frequency `omega` of the regularised oscillator; the last steps are solved for so
that the physical time lands exactly on `dt`). `pert(x, v, tau)` is the perturbing relative
acceleration at elapsed time `tau`. Returns the relative position and velocity.

# Errors
Fails for a non-positive `dt`, `mu` or `eta`, or a collision (`r = 0`).

KS map of a regular state: returns `(u, u')` for position `x` and velocity `v`
(`u'` is the derivative with respect to the fictitious time `ds = dt / r`).

Propagates a (perturbed) Kepler problem in KS variables with RK4.

Propagates a (perturbed) Kepler problem with gravitational parameter 1 in KS
variables with RK4 in the fictitious time `s`, for `n` steps of size `ds`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_rattle_step` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/symplectic/rigid-body/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Bool
```

Actual native geometric operation; physical rigid-body moments/torques use explicit positive SI M/L/T references, while orientations and composition coefficients are dimensionless.

One **implicit RATTLE-type** step with a space-frame torque: the discrete rigid-body
(Moser-Veselov) free step, in which the rotation increment `F` solves the implicit
constraint equation `F J - J F^T = h Pi^` (`J = tr(I)/2 - I` in the principal frame,
Newton iteration), sandwiched between half kicks of the torque. The map is symplectic,
time reversible and second order; it conserves the space-frame angular momentum exactly
in the absence of torque and keeps `R^T R = 1` to round-off.

# Errors
Fails if the Newton iteration for the rotation increment does not converge (very large
steps) or a principal moment is not positive.


Exact flow for time `h` of the **symmetric top** obtained by replacing the two inverse
moments about the axes other than `ax` with their mean: `L` is constant in space, so

`q_ax` a rotation about the symmetry axis by `h L_ax (1/I_ax - 1/I_perp)`.

One Gragg-Bulirsch-Stoer extrapolated step of the time-transformed leapfrog.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_ttl_step` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/symplectic/ttl/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int) -> Float
```

Actual native ttl_step with a true native tape reverse gradient of the physical negative potential. Binding has energy units and may be negative when initial T+B>0; fictitious step has energy*time units; the returned error is explicitly in the native normalized state metric.

Time-transformed leapfrog for `H = T(p) + V(q)` with `V < 0`.

Uses the extended Hamiltonian `K = ln(T + B) - ln(-V)` with `B = -E0`
(`E0` the energy to preserve); the fictitious step `h` corresponds to the
physical step `h / (T + B)`, which is `h r / (GM)` for Kepler (a Sundman
transformation `dt = r ds`). The scheme is symmetric and symplectic in
the extended phase space. `mass` holds one mass per coordinate;
`potential_grad(q, g)` writes `grad V` and returns `V`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_symplectic_ttl_step_composed` (Experimental)


Actual native ttl_step_composed with a true native tape reverse gradient of the physical negative potential. Binding has energy units and may be negative when initial T+B>0; fictitious step has energy*time units; the returned error is explicitly in the native normalized state metric.

Time-transformed leapfrog composed to an even `order`.

Time-transformed leapfrog composed to the even `order` (4, 6, 8, ...): the TTL step is a
symmetric second-order integrator of the extended Hamiltonian `ln(T + B) - ln(-V)`, so
composition with [`composition_weights`] removes the `O(h^2)` energy error of the plain scheme.

# Errors
Fails for an invalid `order`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_transforms_fft` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Complex[_]>
```

Native transforms fft; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Computes the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) of a sequence of complex numbers.

Works at any length and leaves the length unchanged using a shared,
runtime-selected SIMD FFT plan from [`super::fft`].

# Arguments
* `data` - A mutable slice of `Complex<f64>` representing the input sequence.

# Example
```rust
use num_complex::Complex;
use rssn::kernels::transforms::fft;

let mut data = vec![
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(0.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(0.0, 0.0),
];

fft(&mut data);

assert!((data[0].re - 2.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

A length that is not a power of two keeps its length:
```rust
use num_complex::Complex;
use rssn::kernels::transforms::fft;

let mut data = vec![Complex::new(1.0, 0.0); 3];

fft(&mut data);

assert_eq!(data.len(), 3);
// [3, 0, 0] for a constant signal.
assert!((data[0].re - 3.0).abs() < 1e-12);
```

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_transforms_fft_many_par` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Complex[_]>, Int) -> Tensor<2, Complex[_]>
```

Native transforms fft_many_par; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Forward FFT of every row, concurrently, in row order.

Each row runs the serial [`fft`] kernel and only different rows run
concurrently, so the result is bit-identical to transforming the rows one at
a time and therefore independent of the thread count. Fewer than `grain`
rows (or `grain < 2`) run sequentially, so a small batch does not pay for the
task spawn. Use the batch entry point instead of a hand-written `rayon` map
when the rows are independent (the usual row/column pass of a 2-D transform).

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_transforms_fft_slice` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Complex[_]>
```

Native transforms fft_slice; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Computes the Forward FFT for a slice.

**Use this for efficient, parallel chunk processing (e.g., with rayon).**
Works at any length and operates in place: a power-of-two length uses the
scalar radix-2 kernel and other lengths use the shared FFT planner.
Bit-identical to [`fft`].

# Arguments
* `data` - A mutable slice of `Complex<f64>` representing the input sequence.

# Example
```rust
use num_complex::Complex;
use rssn::kernels::transforms::fft_slice;

let mut data = vec![
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(1.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(0.0, 0.0),
    Complex::new(0.0, 0.0),
];

fft_slice(&mut data);

assert!((data[0].re - 2.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_transforms_ifft` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Complex[_]>
```

Native transforms ifft; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Computes the Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT).

Works at any length and leaves the length unchanged, so `ifft(fft(x))`
returns `x` at every length. The `1/n` normalisation is included.

# Arguments
* `data` - A mutable `Vec<Complex<f64>>` representing the input frequency-domain sequence.

# Example
```rust
use num_complex::Complex;
use rssn::kernels::transforms::fft;
use rssn::kernels::transforms::ifft;

let mut data = vec![Complex::new(1.0, 2.0), Complex::new(3.0, 4.0)];

let original = data.clone();

fft(&mut data);

ifft(&mut data);

assert!((data[0].re - original[0].re).abs() < 1e-9);

assert!((data[0].im - original[0].im).abs() < 1e-9);
```

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_dwt` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, String) -> { item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }
```

Native wavelets dwt; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

One level of the periodised discrete wavelet transform: returns `(approximation, detail)`.

`a[k] = sum_m h~[m] x[(2k + m) mod n]`, `d[k] = sum_m g~[m] x[(2k + m) mod n]` with the
analysis banks. An even signal of length `n` maps to `n/2` coefficients of each kind. For odd
lengths or another boundary rule use [`dwt_with`].

# Errors
[`WaveletError::OddLength`] for an empty or odd-length signal.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_dwt2` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Int, String, String) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>
```

Native wavelets dwt2; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

One level of the separable two-dimensional transform, `x` row-major with `rows x cols` entries.

The rows are transformed first, then the columns, and the four sub-bands are packed into a
`(2*ra) x (2*ca)` row-major array with `ra = w.coeff_len(rows, b)` and
`ca = w.coeff_len(cols, b)`: `LL` at rows `0..ra`, columns `0..ca`; `LH` at rows `0..ra`,
columns `ca..2ca`; `HL` at rows `ra..2ra`, columns `0..ca`; `HH` at rows `ra..2ra`, columns
`ca..2ca`. In each label, the first letter gives the filter within each row (horizontal)
and the second the filter within each column (vertical).

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when `rows * cols` does not match `x.len()`, or when a row or column
transform fails.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_method_coeff_len` (Experimental)

```aevia
(String, Int, String) -> Int
```

Native wavelets method_coeff_len; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

The number of coefficients [`dwt_with`] returns for a signal of length `n`.

`ceil(n/2)` in [`Boundary::Periodic`] mode, and `j_hi - j_lo + 1` — about
`n/2 + (m_hi - m_lo)/2` — in the extension modes, where `[m_lo, m_hi]` is the support of
the synthesis banks (see the module documentation).

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_wavedec` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, String, Int) -> { data: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int> }
```

Native wavelets wavedec; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Multilevel decomposition: `[approximation_L, detail_L, ..., detail_1]`.

Requires `2^levels` to divide the length, as before; use [`wavedec_with`] for the general case.

# Errors
[`WaveletError::TooManyLevels`] when `2^levels` does not divide the length, or the length is
shorter than the filter at some level.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_wavedec2` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Int, String, Int) -> { data: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int> }
```

Native wavelets wavedec2; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Multilevel separable two-dimensional decomposition: `[LL_L, packed_L, ..., packed_1]`.

Every level applies [`dwt2`] to the current `LL` band and keeps the whole packed array
(`LL`, `LH`, `HL`, `HH`) for the inverse; the next level then transforms the extracted `LL`
band. The arrays therefore follow the [`wavedec`] convention: the first array is the final
approximation and the remaining ones are the details of the levels from coarsest to finest.
The periodic transform requires the dyadic shape `2^levels | rows` and `2^levels | cols` (the
sizes halve exactly at every level); use [`wavedec2_with`] for another [`Boundary`] mode or a
non-dyadic shape.

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when `rows * cols` does not match `x.len()` or a dimension is zero;
[`WaveletError::TooManyLevels`] when `levels` is zero or exceeds the dyadic depth.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_wavedec2_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Int, String, Int, String) -> { data: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int> }
```

Native wavelets wavedec2_with; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Multilevel separable two-dimensional decomposition with an explicit [`Boundary`] mode.

The recursion is the same as in [`wavedec2`], but any shape is accepted as long as every level
strictly shrinks the approximation band in both dimensions. The extension modes return about
`n/2 + (m_hi - m_lo)/2` coefficients, so once the filters reach the whole band the count stops
shrinking; that is detected per level and reported as [`WaveletError::TooManyLevels`] instead
of recursing on a band that does not get smaller.

# Errors
[`WaveletError::Shape`] when `rows * cols` does not match `x.len()` or a dimension is zero;
[`WaveletError::TooManyLevels`] when `levels` is zero, or a level would not shrink the
approximation.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_wavedec_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, String, Int, String) -> { data: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int> }
```

Native wavelets wavedec_with; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Multilevel decomposition with a [`Boundary`] mode, for any non-empty signal.

Every level keeps the number of coefficients that [`Wavelet::coeff_len`] reports for its
length and `b`, so the levels stop
shrinking once the length is comparable to the filter length (see the module documentation).

# Errors
[`WaveletError::TooManyLevels`] when `levels` is zero or `2^(levels-1) > x.len()`.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_wavelets_waverec2_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ data: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, offsets: Tensor<1, Int> }, Int, Int, String, String) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>
```

Native wavelets waverec2_with; normalized dimensionless arguments unless the declared contract preserves measured signal units. Enum arguments use exact Rust variant names.

Inverse of [`wavedec2_with`]; `rows` and `cols` are the shape of the decomposed array.

The shape of every level is recomputed from `rows`, `cols` and the mode, exactly like
[`waverec_with`]; the `LL` band of each stored level is overwritten with the reconstruction of
the next finer level and [`idwt2`] recovers its input.

# Errors

shape chain does not fit `rows x cols` and the mode.

## `numerical_vector.num_analysis_yee_energy` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/analysis/yee/solver/v1) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native Yee FDTD operation. Explicit positive SI length, wave-speed, impedance and electric-field references define c=epsilon0=mu0=1native coordinates. H uses E/Z, time L/c, energy E²L³/(Zc), conductivity1/(ZL). Grid≤4096and source/work bounds precede execution.

Conserved energy: `½ Σ (ε∞ E² + H²) ΔV` and, for a dispersive medium,
the oscillator energy `Σ (P_t² + ω0² P²) / (2 a) ΔV` of every pole,
both taken at `n - 1/2`. Without poles and without ohmic conduction
this is the electromagnetic energy alone; with conduction it excludes
the dissipated part, which accumulates in [`Yee::ohmic_loss`].

`E` sits at `n` and `H` at `n + 1/2`, so the estimator itself wobbles
at `O(ω dt)` (a few per cent on a coarse grid) even where the discrete
scheme conserves energy exactly; the mean over a period is constant.


Value of the `i`-th B-spline basis function at `x`.

Uses the Cox–de Boor recurrence on non-decreasing knots, with
right-continuous spans and a closed last span. An invalid index or a
non-finite local knot gives NaN.

## `numerical_vector.num_approx_bspline_eval` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Evaluates a B-spline curve `sum c_i B_{i,p}(x)` by de Boor's algorithm.

Requires finite, non-decreasing `knots`, `degree < coeffs.len()` and
`knots.len() == coeffs.len() + degree + 1`. The coordinate is clamped to
the valid range. Returns NaN for an invalid shape or endpoint.

## `numerical_vector.num_approx_bspline_interpolate` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int) -> { item0: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, item1: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }
```

Fits an interpolating B-spline and returns `(knots, coefficients)`.

Degree zero places boundaries at the midpoints between consecutive sites.
Higher degrees use a clamped knot vector with averaged interior knots.

# Errors
[`ApproxError::Invalid`] for inconsistent or non-finite samples, an
invalid degree, unordered sites, or an unrepresentable final degree-zero
interval. [`ApproxError::Singular`] if the collocation system is singular
or overflows.

Session-owned native backend/compiled/scalar handles. Compile an elementary ASCII expression in declared symbol order, normalized by positive physical coordinate references and a positive output reference. Scalar-value handles preserve mixed dimensions individually; call columns are [arity,rows] handles, not mixed-unit numeric tensors. Kind/session/lifetime and units are checked; release invalidates every handle copy.

```aevia
(Float) -> Float
```

Same method and accuracy as [`bessel_i0`].

## `numerical_special.num_bessel_j0` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float) -> Float
```

Bessel J of order zero.

Computes the Bessel function of the first kind, J₀(x).

Accurate to roughly 1e-15 (absolute): power series for |x| < 5, Miller
backward recurrence for 5 ≤ |x| ≤ 25 and the Hankel asymptotic expansion
beyond.



## `numerical_special.num_bessel_y0` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float) -> Float
```

Bessel Y of order zero.

Computes the Bessel function of the second kind, Y₀(x), for x ≥ 0
(`NaN` for x < 0, `-∞` at 0).

Series (A&S 9.1.13) for x < 5, the Neumann expansion
`Y₀ = (2/π)(ln(x/2) + γ) J₀ - (4/π) Σ (-1)^k J_{2k}/k` (A&S 9.1.88) for
5 ≤ x ≤ 25 and the Hankel expansion beyond; accurate to about 1e-14.

## `numerical_special.num_bessel_y1` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float) -> Float
```

Bessel Y of order one.

Computes the Bessel function of the second kind, Y₁(x), for x ≥ 0
(`NaN` for x < 0, `-∞` at 0).

Series (A&S 9.1.11) for x < 5; for 5 ≤ x ≤ 25 the derivative of the
Neumann expansion of Y₀ (`Y₁ = -Y₀'`, `J₀' = -J₁`,
`J_{2k}' = (J_{2k-1} - J_{2k+1})/2`); Hankel expansion beyond.
Accurate to about 1e-14.

## `numerical_callback.num_bfgs` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float>) -> Float, (Tensor<1, Float>) -> Tensor<1, Float>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float>, value: Float, iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, converged: Bool }
```

Dimensionless serial optimization: initial vector,[lower bounds,upper bounds for lbfgs_b],positive tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,objective callback,gradient callback. Both callbacks share a strict evaluation budget. Gradient length matches initial vector; L-BFGS methods retain ten correction pairs. Returns x,value,iterations,evaluations,converged; callback failures propagate unchanged.

BFGS quasi-Newton method with a weak-Wolfe line search. If `grad` is
`None` a central-difference gradient is used.

## `numerical_callback.num_bfgs_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, { coordinate_scale: Float[_], value_scale: Float[_], tolerance: Float, max_iterations: Int, max_evaluations: Int }, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_], (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, converged: Bool, value: Float[_] }
```

Measured nonlinear problem with explicit coordinate_scale and value_scale, dimensionless tolerance, max_iterations and max_evaluations controls. Solves in normalized coordinates/residuals. Arguments: initial, controls, optional lower/upper, objective/residual, optional gradient. Gradient units are objective/coordinate. Homogeneous coordinate and residual vectors; callback failures propagate and budgets are shared.

BFGS quasi-Newton method with a weak-Wolfe line search. If `grad` is
`None` a central-difference gradient is used.

```aevia
(Int, Int) -> Float
```

Floating-point binomial coefficient; returns zero when k exceeds n.

Computes the binomial coefficient C(n, k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!)

## `numerical_callback.num_bootstrap` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_]) -> { estimate: Float[_], mean: Float[_], std_error: Float[_], ci_low: Float[_], ci_high: Float[_], replicates: Tensor<1, Float[_]> }
```

Seeded nonparametric bootstrap: sample vector, positive replicate count, nonnegative u64 seed, statistic-evaluation budget, statistic callback. The callback accepts a sample-unit vector and returns a finite scalar with independently declared statistic units; every summary/replicate retains those units. Budget must cover the original estimate and every replicate. Work is capped at 100000000 resampled entries and storage at 8388608 values. Percentile confidence bounds are 95 percent and are statistical estimates, not coverage guarantees.

Non-parametric bootstrap resampling with `n_resamples` draws.

# Errors

[`StatsExtError::Empty`] when `samples` is empty, [`StatsExtError::Domain`]
when the resample count is zero or cannot be allocated, a uniform draw is
outside `[0, 1)`, or a statistic is non-finite. Callback errors propagate.

## `numerical_callback.num_brent` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { root: Float[_], evaluations: Int }
```

Serial bracketed Brent root solver: lower bound, upper bound, positive argument tolerance, positive iteration budget, callback. The root and tolerance have callback-domain dimensions; residual dimensions are independent. Returns root/evaluations without an extra residual evaluation. Endpoint samples count as evaluations, callback failures propagate unchanged, and iteration exhaustion is an explicit error.

Brent's method on a bracketing interval `[a, b]`.

# Errors
[`RootError::NotBracketed`] if the endpoints have the same nonzero sign,
[`RootError::Invalid`] for non-finite inputs, non-positive tolerance, or
non-finite callback values, and [`RootError::NoConvergence`] at the limit.

## `numerical_callback.num_brent_with_bracket` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { root: Float[_], evaluations: Int, bracket: Tensor<[2], Float[_]> }
```

Bracketed Brent root solver returning the root, actual evaluation count and final two endpoints in ascending order. The argument tolerance and all returned coordinates use the callback's input dimension. An exact zero repeats its coordinate at both endpoints.

## `numerical_callback.num_broyden` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float>) -> Tensor<1, Float>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float>, evaluations: Int }
```

Dimensionless nonlinear system solver: initial vector,positive tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,residual callback. Callback input and output retain the initial vector length. Returns x,evaluations; callback failures and iteration exhaustion are explicit errors.

Broyden's "good" method: finite-difference Jacobian at the start, then
rank-one updates of its inverse-applied form (Sherman-Morrison on `B`).

# Errors
As [`newton_system`].

## `numerical_vector.num_bvh_build` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<2, Float[_]>) -> { payload: rssn/bvh-defining-data/v1, coordinate_unit: Float[_] }
```

Build immutable portable BVH defining data from same-unit N x 3 lower/upper corner tensors. Payload kind rssn/bvh-defining-data/v1 stores only canonical finite corner rows, never pointers or internal tree nodes. Queries validate/version-check the payload and reconstruct the native tree; portable reconstruction is limited to one million work-array coefficients.


Nearest AABB on a portable BVH. Query coordinates share the descriptor's coordinate units; index/distance tensors have zero or one entry, with measured distances. An empty definition gives empty results.

Returns `(aabb_index, distance)` for the [`Aabb`] closest to `point`.
If its distance overflows `f64`, the index remains the nearest and
the distance is positive infinity.

## `numerical_vector.num_cauchy_root_bound` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Float
```

Classic Cauchy upper bound from a complex coefficient vector in ascending order. Coefficients may share ordinate units. The polynomial coordinate and the result are dimensionless.

Classic Cauchy upper bound on the modulus of all roots of
$p(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n `c_k` z^k$ (ascending coefficients):
$R = 1 + \max_{0 \le k < n} |`c_k` / `c_n`|$.

## `numerical_vector.num_cauchy_sharp_root_bound` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Complex[_]>) -> Float
```

Compute the sharp Cauchy radius from ascending complex coefficients with a common ordinate dimension. Returns zero for a nonconstant monomial. The polynomial coordinate and the result are dimensionless.

Computes the sharp Cauchy radius, the positive solution of
$|`c_n`| R^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} |`c_k`| R^k$ for a non-monomial polynomial.
Coefficients are ascending. A monomial has radius zero.


Dimension-aware serial quadrature with a strict callback evaluation budget. Fixed rules: a,b,order,max_evaluations,callback. Romberg/tanh-sinh: a,b,tolerance,max_levels,max_evaluations,callback. Semi-infinite rules: finite_bound,tolerance,max_evaluations,callback; left-infinite integrates (-infinity,bound], right-infinite [bound,infinity). Full infinite rule: tolerance,max_evaluations,callback. Adaptive results include value,error,evaluations,converged; fixed rules report value,evaluations. Callback failures propagate unchanged.

## `numerical_special.num_combinatorics_solve_recurrence_numerical` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Int) -> Float
```

Numerically solves a linear recurrence relation by unrolling it.

The recurrence relation is assumed to be of the form:
`a_n = coeffs[0]*a_{n-1} + coeffs[1]*a_{n-2} + ... + coeffs[order-1]*a_{n-order}`.

# Arguments
* `coeffs` - A slice of `f64` representing the coefficients of the recurrence relation.
* `initial_conditions` - A slice of `f64` representing the initial values `a_0, a_1, ..., a_{order-1}`.
* `target_n` - The index `n` for which to compute `a_n`.

# Returns
A `Result` containing the numerical value of `a_n`.

# Errors

Returns an error if:
- The number of initial conditions does not match the order of the recurrence.
- The internal storage fails to compute values (e.g., empty result vector).

## `numerical_special.num_combinatorics_stirling_second` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Int, Int) -> Float
```

Computes the Stirling number of the second kind `S(n, k)` as an `f64`.

Counts partitions of `n` elements into `k` nonempty subsets. The empty
set has one partition into zero subsets. Returns zero for `k > n` and
for `k = 0 < n`, and positive infinity when the count overflows `f64`.

## `numerical_callback.num_complex_cauchy_derivative_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Complex[_], Float[_], Int, Int, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Complex[_]) -> Complex[_]) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native complex analysis with positive coordinate/value scales, independent D/E physical units and a shared actual callback budget. Circle/residue/count: center,radius,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Contour: path,panels,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Derivative: z,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Newton: z,xscale,yscale,tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,f,df. Cauchy: z,radius,order,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f; dynamic result explicitly retains exact E/D^order units. Analyticity and contour isolation are caller assumptions; native singular/nonconvergence outcomes remain errors.

`f^(n)(z) = n! / (2 pi i) ∮ f(w) / (w - z)^(n+1) dw` over the circle of
`radius` around `z` (Cauchy's integral formula); accurate for high
orders where finite differences are not.


Native complex analysis with positive coordinate/value scales, independent D/E physical units and a shared actual callback budget. Circle/residue/count: center,radius,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Contour: path,panels,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Derivative: z,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Newton: z,xscale,yscale,tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,f,df. Cauchy: z,radius,order,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f; dynamic result explicitly retains exact E/D^order units. Analyticity and contour isolation are caller assumptions; native singular/nonconvergence outcomes remain errors.

`∮ f(z) dz` over the circle `|z - center| = radius`, counter-clockwise,
with `n` equally spaced nodes.


Native complex analysis with positive coordinate/value scales, independent D/E physical units and a shared actual callback budget. ## `numerical_callback.num_complex_count_zeros_poles_scaled` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Complex[_], Float[_], Int, Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Complex[_]) -> Complex[_]) -> Int
```

Native complex analysis with positive coordinate/value scales, independent D/E physical units and a shared actual callback budget. Circle/residue/count: center,radius,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Contour: path,panels,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Derivative: z,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f. Newton: z,xscale,yscale,tolerance,max_iterations,max_evaluations,f,df. Cauchy: z,radius,order,n,xscale,yscale,max_evaluations,f; dynamic result explicitly retains exact E/D^order units. Analyticity and contour isolation are caller assumptions; native singular/nonconvergence outcomes remain errors.

The number of zeros minus the number of poles of `f` inside a circle.

The circle is `|z - center| = radius` (argument principle), and the count
is the winding number of the polygon through the sampled values of `f`.
Samples `f` once per node, in counterclockwise order, with at least 64
nodes. Returns `None` if a sampled value is zero or nonfinite or if a
sampled change of argument exceeds `pi / 2`. Undersampling can still
alias a winding whose changes between nodes are not observed.


Returns the winding number about zero of the polygon formed by a rank-one tensor of complex vertices with a common physical dimension. The last vertex connects to the first. Counterclockwise winding is positive. Empty paths and paths through zero return a domain error.
