## `numerical_vector.num_grid_legacy_fvm_advection1` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/legacy-fvm-mesh/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Advances a retained 1D finite-volume mesh with an upwind flux. Supply a one-entry measured Length/Time velocity, a positive measured Time step, an integer step count, and the left and right ghost-cell values in the mesh field dimension. Both ghost values are validated.

CFL must be at most one. The upwind face uses the ghost value on the side from which the flow enters. Step count and cell-step work are bounded.

The measured field is returned in increasing cell order and replaces the retained field on success. An invalid input or unrepresentable output leaves the previous field intact.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_legacy_fvm_advection2` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/legacy-fvm-mesh/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native finite-volume specialization. Measured field, velocity, length and time retain explicit reference units. Sampled initializer arrays and finite boundary masks instantiate generic native functions; masks must cover exterior cells. Returned values update the retained mesh. Native CFL, work and allocation bounds are checked.

Solves the 2D linear advection equation using the Finite Volume Method.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_legacy_fvm_advection3` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/legacy-fvm-mesh/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Advances the retained 3D finite-volume mesh using measured velocity and timestep. The Boolean mask is flat in x-fastest order or shaped [depth, height, width]. True cells are set to zero on each step. Unmarked exterior cells use zero inflow and free outflow. Returns a flat measured field in x-fastest order. CFL and work bounds are checked.

Advances the 3D linear advection equation with first-order upwind fluxes.

The callback marks cells to set to zero on each time step. All other cells
use a zero exterior state at an inflow face and their own state at an
outflow face. The returned values use the mesh's x-fastest storage order.

For stability, choose `dt` so that the sum of the three directional
Courant numbers `dt * |velocity| / spacing` is at most one.

# Panics
Panics if a mesh advanced for at least one step has inconsistent extents
and cell storage.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_legacy_fvm_shallow_water2` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native finite-volume specialization. Measured field, velocity, length and time retain explicit reference units. Sampled initializer arrays and finite boundary masks instantiate generic native functions; masks must cover exterior cells. Returned values update the retained mesh. Native CFL, work and allocation bounds are checked.

2D shallow water equations `h_t + (hu)_x + (hv)_y = 0`, ...

On a grid of `dims = [nx, ny]` cells (flat, `x` fastest) with the Lax-Friedrichs flux and
zero-gradient boundaries. 2D counterpart of [`solve_shallow_water_1d`]; the
numerical viscosity is shared between the two axes (unsplit scheme), so it
smears slightly more than the 1D routine on y-independent data. Stable for
`(|u| + sqrt(g h)) dt (1/dx + 1/dy) <= 1` (roughly).

# Errors
For a length mismatch or non-positive step sizes.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_legacy_fvm_shallow_water3` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Int>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native finite-volume specialization. Measured field, velocity, length and time retain explicit reference units. Sampled initializer arrays and finite boundary masks instantiate generic native functions; masks must cover exterior cells. Returned values update the retained mesh. Native CFL, work and allocation bounds are checked.

3D barotropic shallow-water system `h_t + ∇·(h u) = 0`,
`(h u)_t + ∇·(h u ⊗ u) + ∇(g h²/2) = 0`.

Euler with `γ = 2`, `p = g h²/2` and no
energy equation: the 3D analogue of the planar shallow-water equations.

On a grid of `dims = [nx, ny, nz]` cells (flat, `x` fastest) with the
Lax-Friedrichs flux and zero-gradient boundaries. 3D counterpart of
[`solve_shallow_water_2d`]; the numerical viscosity is shared between the
three axes (unsplit scheme). Stable for
`(|u| + sqrt(g h)) dt (1/dx + 1/dy + 1/dz) <= 1` (roughly).

# Errors
For a length mismatch or non-positive step sizes.

```aevia
(Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Int, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Measured native continuum adapter. Float matrices and mutable borrows use explicit checked tensor inputs and returned values; SI dimensions, grid shape, work/storage bounds and original native methods are preserved.

Solves the 2D Poisson equation `∇²u = f` using Jacobi iteration.

This function implements the Jacobi iterative method to solve the Poisson equation
on a 2D grid with Dirichlet boundary conditions (implicitly handled by the iteration
not updating boundary points). It is suitable for steady-state problems.

# Arguments
* `f` - Source term (2D grid) as a `Matrix<f64>`.
* `u0` - Initial guess for `u` (2D grid) as a `Matrix<f64>`.
* `dx`, `dy` - Grid spacing in x and y directions.
* `max_iter` - Maximum number of iterations.
* `tolerance` - Convergence tolerance for the maximum difference between successive iterations.

# Returns
A `Matrix<f64>` representing the solution `u`.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_open_fraction` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Int) -> Float
```

Returns the dimensionless open fraction along one, two, or three distinct zero-based axes. Normalize the three origin and length slots by the frame's Length reference and supply positive lengths on the active axes.

The compiled field takes three coherent Length coordinates and returns Length. Positive signed distances are open. One active axis uses segment root refinement. Two or three active axes use adaptive subdivision and simplex clipping.

The depth cap is 12 and depth times the number of axes is at most 18. The independent callback budget accepts 1 through 8,388,608 evaluations. Invalid geometry, callback units or arity, nonfinite samples and budget exhaustion produce errors.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_open_length_fraction` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Dyn<term>, Tensor<1, Float>, Int, Float, Int) -> Float
```

Returns the dimensionless open fraction of an axis-aligned segment. Axis indices are zero based. Normalize the three origin coordinates and positive segment length by the frame's Length reference.

The compiled field takes three coherent Length coordinates and returns Length. Positive distances are open. The kernel samples the segment, then bisects intervals where its sampled sign changes.

The callback budget accepts 1 through 8,388,608 evaluations, including refinement. Invalid geometry, callback units or arity, nonfinite samples, and exhausted evaluation budgets produce errors.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_physics_cfd_advection_1d` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Tensor<1, Float>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native transport calculation in the supplied reference frame. Coordinates, velocities, diffusivities and timesteps are explicitly normalized by Length, Time and field references; no measured numeric input is silently erased. Solver work and storage are bounded.

Solves the 1D advection equation `du/dt + c * du/dx = 0` using an explicit finite difference scheme.

This function implements a simple first-order upwind scheme for stability.

# Arguments
* `u0` - Initial condition (vector of `u` values at `t=0`).
* `c` - Advection speed.
* `dx` - Spatial step size.
* `dt` - Time step size.
* `num_steps` - Number of time steps to simulate.

# Returns
A `Vec<Vec<f64>>` where each inner `Vec` is the solution `u` at a given time step.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_physics_cnm_simulate_1d_heat_conduction_cn_scenario` (Experimental)

```aevia

```

# Returns

```aevia

```

Native transport calculation in the supplied reference frame. Coordinates, velocities, diffusivities and timesteps are explicitly normalized by Length, Time and field references; no measured numeric input is silently erased. Solver work and storage are bounded.

Burgers' equation `u_t + Σ_a (u²/2)_{x_a} = 0` on a 1D, 2D or 3D grid.

The cells are stored flat, with x fastest. Uses the multi-dimensional
Lax–Friedrichs flux with equal numerical-viscosity shares per axis and
zero-gradient outflow boundaries. The one-dimensional stencil agrees with
[`solve_burgers_1d`] up to arithmetic roundoff. See
[`solve_burgers_nd_with_boundaries`] for the stability condition.

# Errors
As [`solve_burgers_nd_with_boundaries`].

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_physics_fvm_burgers_nd_with_boundaries` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Int, Tensor<1, String>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Solves the multidimensional Burgers equation by conservative Lax–Friedrichs fluxes. Use a velocity-valued frame. The flat initial field is in units of value_reference with x fastest, spacing in units of length_reference, and dt in units of time_reference. Supply Periodic or Outflow for both faces of each axis. The CFL bound holds separately on each axis. The returned field keeps all three references.

Advances Burgers' equation with a boundary choice for each active axis.

Uses the same Lax–Friedrichs flux on both sides of an interface. A
fully periodic grid conserves the sum of cell averages up to roundoff.
Zero-gradient faces allow the boundary physical flux to leave or enter
the grid. For the equal viscosity shares used here, a sufficient
monotonicity condition is `D * dt * max|u| <= h[a]` on each active axis,
where `D` is the number of axes. At fixed grid spacing, the one-step
limit as `dt` tends to zero retains Lax–Friedrichs averaging.

# Errors
An invalid grid, boundary count, initial field, or step size, or a flux
or state that cannot be represented.

Computes the plane-stress stiffness matrix of one bilinear quadrilateral. Supply four counterclockwise [x,y] rows scaled by the mechanical Length reference, Young's modulus scaled by the stress reference, and a dimensionless Poisson ratio.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_simplex_refine_marked` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/simplex-mesh/v1, Tensor<1, Bool>) -> rssn/native/simplex-mesh/v1
```

Native simplex finite-element method with explicit geometry/time/field references. Diffusivity is normalized by L²/T, reaction by1/T, source by U/T; compiled callbacks use coherent coordinates and retained physical output domains. Mesh/DOF/refinement/callback work bounds are checked.

Refines the cells flagged in `marked` by conforming edge bisection.

Every marked tetrahedron is split at the midpoints of its six edges
into eight tetrahedra. The split is carried out as recursive
bisection: a cell is cut along its longest split edge (ties broken by
vertex indices) and the two halves are cut again until no split edge
is left.
Only midpoints of edges of marked cells are inserted, so an unmarked
neighbour is cut along exactly the edges it shares with marked cells
(**red–green closure**) and a cell without a split edge is kept. Both
cells sharing a face cut that face from the same edge midpoints to the
opposite vertex of the face, hence there are no hanging nodes.
Boundary facets inherit the marker of the parent facet containing
them. The refinement level of every produced cell is one more than the
level of its parent; cells that are not touched keep their level.

In 1D and 2D the same scheme splits a marked cell into 2 or 4 cells.
Entries of `marked` past the last cell are ignored.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_sm_advance_advection_diffusion_3d_modes` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/pde-frame/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Complex>, Tensor<1, Float>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Advance existing unnormalized-forward 3D FFT coefficients with spectral Forward Euler. Data uses x-fastest order and the supplied frame's field reference. Spacing, velocity, diffusivity and time are normalized in the supplied frame. Zero steps or a zero time step preserves the coefficients.

Advances an existing complex Fourier spectrum by the configured Euler steps.

The spectrum uses the unnormalized forward transform of [`fft3d`] and the
same axis order, with x varying fastest, then y, then z. [`ifft3d`]
divides by the grid size on returning to physical space. A zero-step
or zero-time-step call keeps all validated coefficients unchanged.

# Errors
Rejects zero or overflowing extents, mismatched shape, nonfinite data,
invalid spacing or periods, invalid diffusivity or time step, and
nonfinite computed output.
When a call fails, the spectrum stays unchanged.

every mode is multiplied by `exp((-i c·k - D |k|²) t)`.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_solve_helmholtz_multigrid` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/structured-grid/v1, Float, Dyn<term>, Int, { cycle: String, pre: Int, post: Int, max_cycles: Int, tol: Float, coarsest_nodes: Int }) -> rssn/native/continuum-multigrid-result/v1
```

Actual native continuum multigrid free solver with coherent compiled spatial source of field/length² units, retained physical boundary data, and original cycle controls.

Convenience wrapper: solves `-Δu + σu = f(x)` with multigrid.

# Errors
See [`MultigridSolver::new`].

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_solve_poisson_multigrid_nd` (Experimental)

```aevia

```

Actual native ND multigrid wrapper on a zero-origin rectangular grid. Extents and positive spacings are normalized by the retained Length reference; source uses field/length². Original V/W/Fmg controls, boundary conditions, residuals and convergence status are preserved.

Geometric multigrid for `-Δu + σu = f` on a 1D, 2D or 3D grid.

Face conditions may be Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin or periodic; V, W or full
multigrid cycles. Data are stored with `x` fastest.

# Errors
For inconsistent sizes or boundary descriptions.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_solve_static_structural` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/mechanical-system/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Int>, Tensor<1, Float>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native finite-element assembly/structural method in an explicit mechanical frame. Matrices and loads are normalized in the declared DOF references; the energy reference and heterogeneous DOF references determine every physical coefficient. Assembly, geometry, bounds and mutation results are checked before retention.

Solves a static structural problem for displacements.

This function takes the global stiffness matrix, applied forces, and boundary conditions
to solve for the nodal displacements. It modifies the global stiffness matrix and force
vector to incorporate Dirichlet boundary conditions.

# Arguments
* `global_k` - The global stiffness matrix.
* `forces` - The global force vector.
* `fixed_dofs` - A vector of tuples `(node_idx, prescribed_displacement)` for fixed degrees of freedom.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a `Vec<f64>` of nodal displacements, or an error string if the system is singular.

# Errors
Returns an error if the force vector dimension mismatches the stiffness matrix, or if the resulting system is singular.

## `numerical_vector.num_grid_solve_variable_helmholtz` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/structured-grid/v1, Float, Dyn<term>, Int, String, Float, Tensor<1, Float>, String) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native structured PDE method in the grid reference frame; normalized numeric inputs are converted to coherent callback coordinates and checked physical callback output domains. Callback and discretization work are bounded; native boundary errors propagate.

Solves `-∇·(α(x)∇u) + σ u = f` with a node-sampled diffusivity and the
given boundary conditions (`σ` may be negative for the indefinite
Helmholtz equation). The face values of `α` use `averaging`.

# Errors
On a singular problem (e.g. pure Neumann with `σ = 0`), a solver failure,
an absorbing boundary or a bad `alpha`.

## `numerical_vector.num_homology_abelianization` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/homology/presentation/v1) -> { rank: Int, torsion: Tensor<1, Int> }
```

Native exact algebraic topology with session-owned, kind/version checked complex, chain and presentation handles. Complex inputs/exports use CSR offsets/indices. Handles are invalid in other sessions and after release; all objects own their data. Finite construction bounds: 4096 simplices, 12 vertices per simplex, 65536 face/storage words, 256 generators per chain group and 128 x 128 exact matrix elimination. Presentation simplification accepts sixteen generators and 256 input word coefficients with the native 4000-word intermediate limit; product frontiers are bounded to 1048576 coefficient slots. Cubical chains accept 64 pixels; direct cubical Betti accepts 4096. Filtrations carry a canonical value_unit witness verified against stored radius dimensions. Bars use explicit essential flags and zero death placeholders; bottleneck inputs are births/deaths/essential records and unequal essential counts give positive infinity. Products return None on their native simplex limit; malformed inputs and adapter budget exhaustion are errors. Pure source algorithms are invoked in RSSN kernels; opaque payloads contain only session handles, never serialized pointers.

The abelianisation of a presented group: `Z^rank + torsion`.

Handles are invalid in other sessions and after release; all objects own their data. Presentation simplification accepts sixteen generators and 256 input word coefficients with the native 4000-word intermediate limit; product frontiers are bounded to 1048576 coefficient slots. Cubical chains accept 64 pixels; direct cubical Betti accepts 4096. Filtrations carry a canonical value_unit witness verified against stored radius dimensions. Bars use explicit essential flags and zero death placeholders; bottleneck inputs are births/deaths/essential records and unequal essential counts give positive infinity. Products return None on their native simplex limit; malformed inputs and adapter budget exhaustion are errors. ```

Finite construction bounds: 4096 simplices, 12 vertices per simplex, 65536 face/storage words, 256 generators per chain group and 128 x 128 exact matrix elimination. Presentation simplification accepts sixteen generators and 256 input word coefficients with the native 4000-word intermediate limit; product frontiers are bounded to 1048576 coefficient slots. Cubical chains accept 64 pixels; direct cubical Betti accepts 4096. Filtrations carry a canonical value_unit witness verified against stored radius dimensions. Bars use explicit essential flags and zero death placeholders; bottleneck inputs are births/deaths/essential records and unequal essential counts give positive infinity. Products return None on their native simplex limit; malformed inputs and adapter budget exhaustion are errors. Pure source algorithms are invoked in RSSN kernels; opaque payloads contain only session handles, never serialized pointers.

`H^k(C; Z)` by the universal coefficient theorem: the free part of
`H_k` and the torsion of `H_{k-1}`.

Checks the Mayer-Vietoris sequence of `A ∪ B` at the level of ranks.

the Euler characteristics add up, and there are nonnegative ranks of the
connecting maps that make every stretch of the long exact sequence
exact. Returns the ranks of the connecting maps `H_k(A ∪ B) -> H_{k-1}(A ∩ B)`
for `k = 1 ..` when the check passes.

Persistent homology over `Z/2` of a filtered complex.

The input is
`(value, simplex)` pairs (any order; every face of a simplex must be
present with a value no larger). Bars of dimension up to `max_dim`
with positive length are returned, sorted by dimension, birth, death.

ordered by (value, dimension, lexicographic), are reduced from left to
right until their lowest ones are distinct.

## `numerical_vector.num_homology_projective_plane` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Int) -> rssn/native/homology/complex/v1
```

Native exact algebraic topology with session-owned, kind/version checked complex, chain and presentation handles. Complex inputs/exports use CSR offsets/indices. Handles are invalid in other sessions and after release; all objects own their data. Finite construction bounds: 4096 simplices, 12 vertices per simplex, 65536 face/storage words, 256 generators per chain group and 128 x 128 exact matrix elimination. Presentation simplification accepts sixteen generators and 256 input word coefficients with the native 4000-word intermediate limit; product frontiers are bounded to 1048576 coefficient slots. Cubical chains accept 64 pixels; direct cubical Betti accepts 4096. Filtrations carry a canonical value_unit witness verified against stored radius dimensions. Bars use explicit essential flags and zero death placeholders; bottleneck inputs are births/deaths/essential records and unequal essential counts give positive infinity. Products return None on their native simplex limit; malformed inputs and adapter budget exhaustion are errors. Pure source algorithms are invoked in RSSN kernels; opaque payloads contain only session handles, never serialized pointers.

A triangulation of the real projective plane: for `k = 0` the minimal
one with 6 vertices; for `k >= 3` a disc with `2k` boundary edges whose
antipodal boundary points are identified (word `a a`).

## `numerical_vector.num_homology_rank_mod_p` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Int>, Int) -> Int
```

Return the rank of a rectangular integer matrix of at most 128 by 128 over a prime field. The modulus is an exact prime in the unsigned 64-bit range. Negative entries and characteristic two are supported.

The rank of a rectangular integer matrix over the field with prime
modulus `p`. Binary elimination packs 64 columns into each machine word.

# Panics
Panics for ragged rows or a modulus below two. The caller must supply a prime.

## `numerical_callback.num_integrate` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Float[_], Float[_], Float, Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], error: Float[_], evaluations: Int, converged: Bool }
```

Serial adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature: a, b, absolute tolerance, relative tolerance, max panels, callback. Returns value/error/evaluations/converged. Bounds match the callback domain; value/error/absolute tolerance carry domain times codomain dimensions; zero absolute tolerance is polymorphic. Callback errors propagate unchanged, and the estimate is heuristic, not a rigorous enclosure.

Adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration of `f` over `[a, b]`.

The interval with the largest error estimate is bisected until the total
error is below `max(abs_tol, rel_tol * |value|)` or `max_panels` panels
exist. An unconverged refinement may use Wynn extrapolation of recent
totals. Cancellation is checked between panels and stops refinement with
`converged = false`. The first panel is evaluated even if `max_panels` is zero.

## `numerical_callback.num_integrate_infinite` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], evaluations: Int, error: Float[_], converged: Bool }
```

Dimension-aware serial quadrature with a strict callback evaluation budget. Fixed rules: a,b,order,max_evaluations,callback. Romberg/tanh-sinh: a,b,tolerance,max_levels,max_evaluations,callback. Semi-infinite rules: finite_bound,tolerance,max_evaluations,callback; left-infinite integrates (-infinity,bound], right-infinite [bound,infinity). Full infinite rule: tolerance,max_evaluations,callback. Adaptive results include value,error,evaluations,converged; fixed rules report value,evaluations. Callback failures propagate unchanged.

Integral over `(-inf, inf)` using `x = t/(1-t^2)`, `t in (-1, 1)`.

## `numerical_callback.num_integrate_left_infinite` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], evaluations: Int, error: Float[_], converged: Bool }
```

Dimension-aware serial quadrature with a strict callback evaluation budget. Fixed rules: a,b,order,max_evaluations,callback. Romberg/tanh-sinh: a,b,tolerance,max_levels,max_evaluations,callback. Semi-infinite rules: finite_bound,tolerance,max_evaluations,callback; left-infinite integrates (-infinity,bound], right-infinite [bound,infinity). Full infinite rule: tolerance,max_evaluations,callback. Adaptive results include value,error,evaluations,converged; fixed rules report value,evaluations. Callback failures propagate unchanged.

Integral over `[a, inf)` using `x = a + t/(1-t)`, `t in [0, 1)`.

## `numerical_callback.num_integrate_semi_infinite` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float[_], Float[_], Int, (Float[_]) -> Float[_]) -> { value: Float[_], evaluations: Int, error: Float[_], converged: Bool }
```

Dimension-aware serial quadrature with a strict callback evaluation budget. Fixed rules: a,b,order,max_evaluations,callback. Romberg/tanh-sinh: a,b,tolerance,max_levels,max_evaluations,callback. Semi-infinite rules: finite_bound,tolerance,max_evaluations,callback; left-infinite integrates (-infinity,bound], right-infinite [bound,infinity). Full infinite rule: tolerance,max_evaluations,callback. Adaptive results include value,error,evaluations,converged; fixed rules report value,evaluations. Callback failures propagate unchanged.

Integral over `[a, inf)` using `x = a + t/(1-t)`, `t in [0, 1)`.

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_akima` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Akima 1D cubic spline interpolation.

[Akima's local slope weights](https://doi.org/10.1145/321607.321609)
reduce oscillation near sharp corners. Queries outside the sampled interval
extend the nearest segment's polynomial. One sample defines a constant and
two samples define a line.

# Errors
Unequal sample lengths, empty samples, non-finite inputs, non-increasing
knots, or local arithmetic outside the `f64` range.

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_akima_many` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>
```

Evaluates an Akima interpolant at multiple coordinates, preserving query order.

Uses the same knot and extrapolation rules as [`akima`]. Successive queries
in the same segment reuse its coefficients. Duplicate queries are allowed.
An empty query list returns an empty vector after validating the samples.

# Errors
Unequal sample lengths, empty samples, non-finite inputs, non-increasing
knots, local arithmetic outside the `f64` range, or an unavailable output
allocation.

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Bicubic interpolation on a rectilinear 2D grid.

`grid` is row-major of length `ys.len() * xs.len()` where `grid[j * xs.len() + i]`
is the value at `(xs[i], ys[j])`.

# Errors
[`InterpError::ShapeMismatch`], [`InterpError::Empty`], or [`InterpError::Domain`].

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_bspline_eval` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int, Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Evaluates a B-spline of given `degree` at `x` using de Boor's algorithm.

Requires `knots.len() == coeffs.len() + degree + 1`, non-decreasing `knots`,
and positive-width support. Queries outside the support are clamped to
its endpoints.

# Errors
[`InterpError::ShapeMismatch`] or [`InterpError::Domain`].

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>
```

The monomial coefficients of the polynomial interpolating `(xs, ys)` at `degree + 1` Chebyshev nodes of the sample's range.

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_interp1` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Linear interpolation of `(xs, ys)` at `x`.

Outside the range the nearest endpoint is extended linearly from its own
segment, which is what a piecewise-linear interpolant does at its ends.

# Errors

[`InterpError::ShapeMismatch`] when the two samples differ in length, and
[`InterpError::Empty`] when there are no points.

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_interp2` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Bilinear interpolation on a rectilinear grid.

`grid` is `ny × nx` in row-major order, with `xs` varying fastest.
Finite coordinates outside the grid are clamped to its edges.
Use [`BilinearGrid`] to reuse validation across a series of queries.

# Errors

Rejects empty or invalid axes, mismatched grid storage, and non-finite
grid values or queries.

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_interpn` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Float[_]
```

N-dimensional multilinear interpolation on a rectilinear grid.

`axes[d]` gives the strictly increasing coordinates along axis `d`,
`grid` is row-major of length `prod(axes[d].len())`, and `point` has length `axes.len()`.

[`InterpError::ShapeMismatch`], [`InterpError::Empty`], or [`InterpError::Domain`].

Computes the `[m / n]` Padé approximant `P(x) / Q(x)` from Taylor series coefficients `coeffs[0..=m+n]` (ascending power order).

## `numerical_vector.num_interp_ext_pchip` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_]) -> Float[_]
```

Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial (PCHIP, Fritsch–Carlson).

Preserves monotonicity of the data without overshoot between knots. Uses
[Fritsch–Butland's weighted harmonic mean](https://doi.org/10.1137/0905021)
for interior tangents and clipped one-sided formulas at the endpoints.
Queries outside the sampled interval extend the nearest segment's polynomial.
One sample defines a constant and two samples define a line.

# Errors
Unequal sample lengths, empty samples, non-finite inputs, non-increasing
knots, or local arithmetic outside the `f64` range.

## `numerical_vector.num_interpolate_b_spline` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>, Int, Tensor<1, Float>, Float) -> None | Some(Tensor<1, Float>)
```

Evaluates a point on a B-spline curve.

B-splines are generalizations of Bézier curves, offering more flexibility and local control.
They are defined by control points, a degree, and a knot vector. This function uses
the Cox-de Boor recursion formula to evaluate the curve at a given parameter `t`.

# Arguments
* `control_points` - The control points.
* `degree` - The degree of the spline, `p`.
* `knots` - The knot vector, `U`.
* `t` - The parameter.

# Returns
The coordinates of the point on the curve.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::b_spline;

let control_points = vec![vec![0.0], vec![1.0], vec![2.0]];

let knots = vec![0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0];

let p = b_spline(&control_points, 2, &knots, 0.5);

assert!((p.unwrap()[0] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

## `numerical_vector.num_interpolate_bezier_curve` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>, Float) -> Tensor<1, Float>
```

Evaluates a point on a Bézier curve defined by a set of control points at parameter `t`.

This function uses De Casteljau's algorithm, a numerically stable and efficient method
for evaluating Bézier curves. The curve passes through the first and last control points
and is tangent to the segments connecting the first two and last two control points.

# Arguments
* `control_points` - A slice of points, where each point is a slice of `f64` coordinates.
* `t` - The parameter, typically in the range `[0, 1]`.

# Returns
The coordinates of the point on the curve.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::bezier_curve;

let control_points = vec![vec![0.0, 0.0], vec![1.0, 2.0], vec![2.0, 0.0]];

let p = bezier_curve(&control_points, 0.5);

assert!((p[0] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);

assert!((p[1] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

## `numerical_special.num_inverse_beta_reg` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float, Float, Float) -> Float
```

`num_inverse_beta_reg(a, b, p)` returns the regularized beta quantile at a probability in [0, 1]. Shape parameters must be finite and positive. The general inversion uses a bounded search and reports nonrepresentable forward evaluations as domain errors.

The inverse of the regularized incomplete beta function.

Returns the `x` in `[0, 1]` such that `I_x(a, b) = p`. Endpoints and
the one-unit-shape cases use their analytic values. Other cases bracket
the quantile in binary64. Reflection gives the upper-tail probability
directly from the forward kernel when `x > 0.5`.

# Errors
The shapes must be finite and positive, and the probability must lie in
`[0, 1]`. A nonrepresentable forward evaluation returns an error.

## `numerical_special.num_inverse_erf` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Float) -> Float
```

Computes the inverse error function, erf⁻¹(x).

Starts from Winitzki's closed-form approximation and polishes with Halley
iterations on `erfc(y) = 1 - x` (for x ≥ 0.5, where `1 - x` is exact and
the tail keeps full relative precision) or on `erf(y) = x` otherwise.

```aevia
(Float) -> { lower: Float, upper: Float }
```

Koebe distortion theorem bounds for $f \in \mathcal{S}$ at $|z| = r \in [0, 1)$:
$\frac{1-r}{(1+r)^3} \le |f'(z)| \le \frac{1+r}{(1-r)^3}$.


Goluzin's sharp upper bound in radians on the absolute continuous argument of f'(z) for |z|=r in [0,1).

Returns Goluzin’s sharp rotation bound on the circle of radius `r`.

Goluzin's sharp rotation theorem bound on $|\arg f'(z)|$ for $f \in \mathcal{S}$ at $|z| = r \in [0, 1)$:
$4 \arcsin(r)$ for $r \le 1/\sqrt{2}$, and $\pi + \ln\frac{r^2}{1 - r^2}$ for $1/\sqrt{2} < r < 1$.


Measured nonlinear problem with explicit coordinate_scale and value_scale, dimensionless tolerance, max_iterations and max_evaluations controls. Solves in normalized coordinates/residuals. ## `numerical_callback.num_least_squares` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Float[_]>, Float[_], Float, Float, Float, Int, Int, (Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> Tensor<1, Float[_]>) -> { x: Tensor<1, Float[_]>, residual_norm: Float[_], iterations: Int, evaluations: Int, jacobian_evaluations: Int, accepted_steps: Int, rejected_steps: Int, converged: Bool, status: String }
```

Damped nonlinear least squares with a scoped vector residual callback. Initial parameters and residuals may have independent dimensions. Returns the best point, residual norm, work counters, convergence and explicit stopping status; callback failures propagate.

Minimise one half of the squared residual norm using a damped, column-scaled
augmented SVD. The Jacobian may be analytic or safely differenced.

The reported scaled gradient is formed from `J[:,j]/max(abs(J[:,j]))` and
`f/max(abs(f))`; it is a dimensionless first-order test, not a root proof.
Trial steps are accepted only on positive actual and predicted decrease.
Residual length must remain constant on every evaluation.

# Errors
Invalid input, malformed callback results, or a failed decomposition return
a [`LeastSquaresError`]. Nonconvergence is reported as a result status.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_anderson` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Dyn<term>, Int, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native low-rank/operator method. Matrices and state arrays retain explicit physical references; orthonormal factors are dimensionless. Shapes, iterations, callbacks and allocations are bounded.

Solves `x = g(x)` by Anderson acceleration with a window of `window`
previous iterates.

Each step mixes the last iterates so that the linearised residual is
smallest in the least-squares sense; with `window = 0` it is the plain
iteration `x <- g(x)`. `damping` in `(0, 1]` scales the step (`1` is the
undamped method). A step whose least-squares problem is degenerate, or
that produces non-finite numbers, falls back to the plain iterate and
restarts the window.

# Errors
[`LowRankError::Shape`] when `g` changes the length of the vector or the
start is not finite; [`LowRankError::NoConvergence`] when the residual is
still above `tol` after `max_evaluations`.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_arnoldi` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Tensor<1, Float>, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Builds a dimensionless Krylov basis and the Hessenberg matrix for the normalized linear operator. The result contains basis, hessenberg, beta and the measured operator_reference. Multiply the Hessenberg coefficients and residual beta by that reference to restore physical units.

Computes a matrix-free Arnoldi factorisation with up to `m` directions.

The operator must overwrite its output slice with `A x`. The return value
`(V, H, beta)` satisfies `A V_m ≈ V_m H + beta v_{m+1} e_m^T`. The first
vector in `V` is the normalised `v0` and the last of its `m + 1` vectors
is the normalised residual direction. `H` is `m x m` and upper Hessenberg.
Iteration stops when the residual is at most `1e-14` times the norm of
the current operator image or when the ambient dimension is exhausted.
Unused vectors and columns are zero-padded, with `beta = 0` after this
breakdown. A zero or empty start gives all zeros and skips the operator.

A non-finite start or operator image, or overflow in a projected
coefficient or residual norm, is signalled by NaN in `beta` and on the
failing diagonal of `H`, if present. Earlier completed columns and basis
vectors are retained.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_berlekamp_massey` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<1, Int>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Int>
```

Native exact sparse/domain operation specialized to BigRational or a validated prime field. Coefficients are normalized dimensionless exact values; finite shape, coefficient-bit and work budgets are enforced.

Berlekamp-Massey: the shortest linear recurrence of a sequence over

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_bicgstab_l` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csr/v1, rssn/native/array/v1, None | Some(Tensor<1, Float>), Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native sparse solver with explicit matrix/RHS reference domains. Solutions retain RHS/matrix units; initial vectors use that normalized solution reference. Native method/preconditioner choices, residuals and convergence reports are preserved; shape and work budgets are checked.

`BiCGSTAB`(`l`) with right preconditioning (`l >= 1`).

`l = 1` is classical `BiCGSTAB`; `l = 2` or more smooths the residual
polynomial with a degree-`l` minimal-residual step, which avoids the
breakdown of `BiCGSTAB` on matrices with strongly complex spectra. The
iteration count is the number of outer cycles started. Each complete cycle
uses `2 l` matrix-vector products, plus the initial and final verification
for the solve.

Convergence is verified against the original system using the requested
nonnegative, finite tolerance. With a zero right-hand side, the reported
relative residual is zero for an exact solution and infinite otherwise.
Both callbacks must overwrite every output entry with finite values.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_bsr_matmul_dense` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/bsr/v1, rssn/native/array/v1) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Multiplies a block sparse matrix by a rank-two array of right-hand sides. The result keeps the product of the operands' reference scales and physical dimensions.

Multiplies a row-major dense matrix of shape `(ncols, rhs_cols)` by
this BSR matrix on the left. Returns row-major `(nrows, rhs_cols)`.
Each output is rounded once from the exact dot product, so running
[`Self::matvec`] on each RHS column gives the same bits.

# Errors
A malformed BSR matrix, a dense operand that disagrees with its given
width, or an unrepresentable or unavailable output allocation.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_bsr_matvec` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/bsr/v1, rssn/native/array/v1) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Native sparse matrix operation with retained entry reference and physical unit domain. Indices are zero based; normalized array storage, capability kind/session and size/work budgets are checked.

Matrix-vector product `y = A x`.

Every entry of `y` is the correctly rounded dot product of its row, so
the result equals [`Csr::matvec`] of [`Bsr::to_csr`] bit for bit,
whatever the block shape; block rows run in parallel for large
matrices without changing a bit. Only the first `min(y.len(), nrows)`
output entries are written.

# Panics
A malformed matrix or an input missing a referenced entry can panic.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_choose_block_size` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csr/v1, Tensor<2, Int>) -> Tensor<1, Int>
```

Native sparse matrix operation with retained entry reference and physical unit domain. Indices are zero based; normalized array storage, capability kind/session and size/work budgets are checked.

Picks the block shape for `csr` among `candidates`.

A candidate qualifies when it divides the matrix shape and its fill ratio
(stored scalars per true nonzero, see [`Bsr::fill_ratio`]) is at most
[`MAX_FILL_RATIO`]. The largest qualifying block wins, ties going to the
lower fill ratio. The result is `(1, 1)` for malformed CSR arrays or
when no candidate qualifies.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_complex_schur` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Complex>, Dyn<term>) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native complex Schur decomposition of normalized coefficients with a positive physical entry reference; q is dimensionless and t uses the retained entry reference.

Complex Schur decomposition `A = Q T Q^H` (`T` upper triangular, `Q`
unitary) of a dense square matrix by Householder reduction to Hessenberg
form and Wilkinson-shifted QR iterations with deflation.

Returns `None` if the iteration does not converge.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_contract` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Int) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Native numerical method. Normalized coordinates and positive physical reference scales are checked; native object kind/session/lifetime and allocation/work budgets are enforced.

Contracts a single tensor along two specified axes (a generalised
trace): the result has rank `ndim - 2` and entries
`sum_t a[..., t, ..., t, ...]`, the remaining axes in their original
order.

# Errors

lengths.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_contract_rectangular` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Int, Int, Int, Float, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Native generic contraction specialized to f64. The compiled scalar callback receives row, inner index, column, has_previous, previous in that order; index/presence inputs are dimensionless and previous/output use the explicit reference dimension. Indices are zero based and coherent physical values are normalized only at the callback boundary.

Compute a rectangular product in row-major, first-product accumulation order.

`accumulate(row, index, column, previous)` performs one scalar product and,
when present, adds it to `previous`. This supports exact, complex and physical
host scalars without importing their runtime representation into the kernel.
Zero-length contractions obtain each additive identity from `zero`.

# Errors
Returns [`ContractionError::ShapeOverflow`] when the output size is invalid
or the allocation fails, or [`ContractionError::Element`] for the first scalar failure.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_cp_als` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, rssn/native/cp-options/v1) -> rssn/native/cp/v1
```

Native tensor decomposition with explicit reference scale and bounded factor/order/sweep storage. Factors are normalized; reconstructed tensors retain the input physical domain.

CP (CANDECOMP/PARAFAC) decomposition by alternating least squares.

Factorises a dense tensor as `T ~= sum_r lambda_r a_r o b_r o c_r` for
`options.rank` components, by solving one matricised least-squares problem
per mode per sweep (the standard ALS update on the mode-`k` unfolding
against the Khatri-Rao product of the other factors). Factors are
initialised uniformly at random from `options.seed` and normalised after
every update, with the removed norms kept in
[`CpDecomposition::weights`].

A rank-`R` tensor whose factors span a full-rank problem is recovered to
rounding error, but the factors themselves are only determined up to
permutation and scaling: compare reconstructions, not factors.

CP is ill-posed, so the result says what happened rather than assuming
success. `converged` means the residual reached `tol`; `stagnated` means
sweeps stopped improving while the residual stayed above `tol`; `diverged`
means a weight blew up, which is how a degenerate problem (border rank
below rank) shows itself; `rank_deficient` means the least-squares system
was numerically rank deficient in its direct SVD solve.

# Errors
Returns an error for a tensor of rank below 2, an empty dimension,
non-finite entries/options, a zero rank, zero sweeps, or rescaling overflow.
Updates solve the Khatri-Rao least-squares system directly by SVD, once
per mode, avoiding normal equations and squared condition numbers. Input
normalization protects uniformly very small or very large tensors.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_csc_cg` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csc/v1, rssn/native/array/v1, None | Some(Tensor<1, Float>), Int, Float) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Actual native CSC sparse kernel with explicit entry reference, preserving historical CSR function names without transposing logical rows/columns. Physical matrix/vector domains and normalized tolerances are checked; work and allocations are bounded.

Solves a sparse linear system `Ax=b` using the Conjugate Gradient method.

This method is suitable for symmetric, positive-definite matrices. It is an iterative
algorithm that converges to the exact solution in at most `n` iterations (where `n` is
the matrix dimension) in exact arithmetic, but is typically stopped earlier based on a tolerance.

The tolerance is an absolute bound on the Euclidean norm of the residual
`b - A x`, checked before the first iteration and after every update. If the
iteration limit is reached without meeting it, the current iterate is
returned anyway. faer 0.24 does ship a conjugate gradient
(`faer::matrix_free::conjugate_gradient`), but it tests a *relative*
residual, reports `NonConvergence` as an error and requires a positive
definite operator, so using it would change all three behaviours; the loop is
kept, iterating over the faer storage.

# Arguments
* `a` - The sparse matrix `A` ([`SparseMat`]).
* `b` - The vector `b` (`Array1<f64>`).
* `x0` - An initial guess for the solution `x`.
* `max_iter` - The maximum number of iterations.
* `tolerance` - The desired tolerance for the residual norm.

# Returns
A `Result` containing the solution vector `x`, or an error string.

# Errors
Returns an error if the matrix and vector dimensions are incompatible.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_csc_matvec` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csc/v1, rssn/native/array/v1) -> rssn/native/array/v1
```

Actual native CSC sparse kernel with explicit entry reference, preserving historical CSR function names without transposing logical rows/columns. Physical matrix/vector domains and normalized tolerances are checked; work and allocations are bounded.

Performs sparse matrix-vector multiplication for a sparse matrix and a standard `Vec`.

The matrix is stored in CSC, so the loop walks columns: every stored entry
contributes `val * vector[column]` to `result[row]`. This is the same
arithmetic as `y[i] = sum_j A[i][j] * x[j]`, but it never needs the transpose
of the matrix.

# Arguments
* `matrix` - The sparse matrix.
* `vector` - The dense vector.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a `Vec<f64>` representing the result of the multiplication.

# Errors
Returns an error if matrix and vector dimensions are not compatible.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_csr_ic0` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csr/v1) -> None | Some(rssn/native/ic0/v1)
```

Native sparse factor/preconditioner with its matrix entry reference. Application returns a normalized result with physical reference RHS/matrix; shapes, unit domains and factor work are checked.

IC(0) factorisation `A ≈ L D L^T` (incomplete Cholesky without fill).

The lower triangular factor uses the strictly lower pattern of `A`;
the upper triangle of `A` is ignored, so the matrix must be symmetric
and positive definite for `M = L D L^T` to be a valid CG
preconditioner. On a symmetric matrix this is the same operator as
[`Csr::ilu0`] written as `L D L^T` instead of `L U`.

# Returns
`None` for malformed CSR, a missing diagonal, a nonpositive pivot,
or unrepresentable lower-triangular factor entries. The factor
stores only the strict lower triangle, its transpose and the pivots.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_csr_ilu0` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/csr/v1) -> None | Some(rssn/native/ilu0/v1)
```

Native sparse factor/preconditioner with its matrix entry reference. Application returns a normalized result with physical reference RHS/matrix; shapes, unit domains and factor work are checked.

ILU(0) factorisation (incomplete LU keeping the sparsity pattern).

The factors are stored in the pattern of `A`: the strictly lower
entries of `L` (unit diagonal) and the entries of `U` in the same
arrays. No fill is created and no pivoting is performed.

# Returns
`None` when the matrix has no entry on the diagonal of some row or
when a zero pivot is met (structurally or after elimination). The
factorisation never returns `NaN`: on `None` the caller keeps the
unpreconditioned path or falls back to [`Csr::jacobi_inverse`].


Native sparse matrix operation with retained entry reference and physical unit domain. Indices are zero based; normalized array storage, capability kind/session and size/work budgets are checked.

Reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering of the symmetrised pattern, with a
George-Liu pseudo-peripheral start vertex per connected component.
Uses the leading `min(rows, cols)` square, with every stored

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_cubic_spline_interpolation` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/interpolation-curve/v1
```

Native interpolation over normalized samples with explicit coordinate and ordinate references. Physical queries and outputs are checked against retained domains; point/order/allocation bounds are enforced.

Creates a cubic spline interpolator for a given set of points.

Cubic spline interpolation constructs a piecewise cubic polynomial that passes
through each data point, ensuring smoothness (continuity of first and second derivatives)
at the interior points. The input points must be sorted by their x-coordinates.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples. Must be sorted by x.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a closure `Arc<dyn Fn(f64) -> f64>` that can be used to evaluate
the spline at any point.

# Errors
Returns an error if fewer than two points are provided, or if the x-coordinates are not strictly increasing.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::cubic_spline_interpolation;

let points = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 0.0)];

let spline = cubic_spline_interpolation(&points).unwrap();

// Check that interpolated value is reasonable (between the y values)
let val = spline(0.5);

assert!((spline(0.5) - 0.6875).abs() < 1e-9);
assert!(val > 0.0 && val < 1.0);
```

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_cubic_spline_with` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, String, Float, Float) -> rssn/native/interpolation-curve/v1
```

Native interpolation over normalized samples with explicit coordinate and ordinate references. Physical queries and outputs are checked against retained domains; point/order/allocation bounds are enforced.

Cubic spline interpolation with a selectable end condition.

Fourth order in the node spacing when the end condition matches the data — clamped
with the exact end slopes, or not-a-knot — and second order for the natural condition,
whose zero end curvature a general smooth function violates. Values outside the node
range are extrapolated with the first or the last cubic.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples with strictly increasing `x`; at least three
  of them, four for [`SplineEnd::NotAKnot`].
* `ends` - The end condition.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a closure `Arc<dyn Fn(f64) -> f64>` evaluating the spline.

# Errors
Returns an error for too few points, non-increasing abscissae, or a singular system.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::SplineEnd;
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::cubic_spline_with;

let points = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 0.0), (3.0, 1.0)];

let spline = cubic_spline_with(&points, SplineEnd::NotAKnot).unwrap();

assert!((spline(1.0) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
```


## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_dense_eigen` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>) -> { values: { item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, vectors: Tensor<2, Complex>, residuals: Tensor<1, Float>, defective: Bool }
```

Checked native linear calculation in normalized reference coordinates. Physical tensors must be explicitly nondimensionalized; normalized outputs use the same declared reference basis.

Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a general (non-symmetric) real matrix.

The matrix is first balanced by an exact power-of-two diagonal similarity,
reduced to upper Hessenberg form by Householder similarities and driven to
real Schur form by the implicitly shifted QR algorithm (Francis double
shift). A complex-conjugate pair of a real matrix therefore appears as a
2x2 diagonal block and is returned as two complex eigenvalues with complex
eigenvectors; the transformation is accumulated, so the vectors belong to
the original matrix. Eigenvectors of the quasi-triangular factor are
obtained by block back substitution.

For a symmetric matrix prefer [`eigen_symmetric`]: it is cheaper and
returns real orthonormal vectors.

A defective matrix (a Jordan block, for instance) has fewer independent
eigenvectors than eigenvalues. This routine returns one vector per
eigenvalue, flags the result through [`Eigen::defective`] and leaves the
dependent vectors parallel; see the module-level limitations.

# Errors
[`DenseError::Shape`] for non-square input, [`DenseError::NoConvergence`]
when a Schur eigenvalue needs more than `200 n` QR sweeps.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_dense_eigen_generalized_symmetric` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>, Tensor<2, Float>) -> { values: { item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, vectors: None | Some(Tensor<2, Float>), b_positive_definite: Bool }
```

Checked native linear calculation in normalized reference coordinates. Physical tensors must be explicitly nondimensionalized; normalized outputs use the same declared reference basis.

Dense symmetric generalised eigenproblem `A x = lambda B x` (`A`, `B` symmetric).

For positive definite `B` (Cholesky `B = L L^T` succeeds) the problem is reduced to the
symmetric `L^{-1} A L^{-T}`; the eigenvalues are real and the eigenvectors `B`-orthonormal.
For **indefinite** `B` the Cholesky reduction does not exist, and the eigenvalues are those of
`B^{-1} A` (LU solve, then the general QR algorithm), which may be complex pairs; no
eigenvectors are returned then.

# Errors
[`DenseError::Shape`] for mismatched or non-square input, [`DenseError::Singular`] when `B`
is indefinite and singular, [`DenseError::NoConvergence`] from the QR iteration.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_gen_shift_invert` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Int, Float, Int, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

General generalised eigenproblem `A x = lambda B x`.

`A` is an arbitrary real matrix and `B` real and nonsingular: the `k`
eigenvalues closest to `opts.sigma` by Krylov-Schur on
`(A - sigma B)^{-1} B`. Eigenvalues may be complex.
The residuals are the absolute 2-norms in the original pencil, as in
[`eigs_gen_sym_shift_invert`].

# Errors
As [`eigs_krylov_schur`].

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_gen_sym_shift_invert` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Int, Float, Int, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

Symmetric generalised eigenproblem `A x = lambda B x` (`A` symmetric,
`B` symmetric, positive definite for the Lanczos path): the `k` eigenvalues closest to
`opts.sigma`.

`solve(x, y)` writes `(A - sigma B)^{-1} x` into `y`. Block Lanczos runs
in the `B` inner product on `(A - sigma B)^{-1} B`, which is self-adjoint
there; `theta` maps back to `lambda = sigma + 1/theta`. The returned
eigenvectors are `B`-orthonormal and `residuals` are the true norms
`||A x - lambda B x||₂`. Convergence uses the Ritz residuals of the
transformed operator. The callbacks write the full action of a linear
map. For a purely real eigenvector the residual requires one application
of each operator.

**Indefinite `B`.** The `B` inner product only exists for positive definite `B`. The
solver first estimates the extreme eigenvalues of `B` by Lanczos
([`b_is_positive_definite`]); when `B` is not (numerically) positive definite it falls
back to [`eigs_gen_shift_invert`] (Krylov-Schur on `(A - sigma B)^{-1} B`, any nonsingular
`B`), whose eigenvalues may be complex pairs and whose eigenvectors are 2-normalised, not
`B`-orthonormal.

# Errors
As [`eigs_sym_block`].

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_jd` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Float, Float, Int, Int, Int, Int, Bool, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

Jacobi-Davidson for the `k` eigenvalues of a general **non-symmetric**
real operator closest to the (complex) `target`, interior eigenvalues
included.

The method works in complex arithmetic with a *partial Schur* deflation:
the search space stays orthogonal to the locked Schur vectors `Q`
(`A Q = Q R`, `R` upper triangular), harmonic Ritz pairs of the pencil
`(W^H V, W^H W)`, `W = (I - Q Q^H)(A - target) V`, are extracted with the
complex Schur decomposition [`complex_schur`], and the correction equation
`(I - Q~ Q~^H)(A - theta)(I - Q~ Q~^H) t = -r` (`Q~ = [Q, u]`) is solved by
complex GMRES, optionally right-preconditioned by `precond`
(`K^{-1}` for a real `K ~ A - theta`, applied to the real and imaginary
parts). Eigenvalues are the diagonal of `R` and the eigenvectors are
`Q y` with `y` the eigenvectors of `R`; `residuals` are true residuals
`|A x - lambda x|`. As in [`eigs_jd_sym`], iteration continues after `k`
locks until no unlocked candidate is closer to the target.

# Errors
[`EigsError::Invalid`] for `k == 0` or `k > n`; [`EigsError::Dense`] if a
projected problem fails.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_jd_sym` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Float, Float, Int, Int, Int, Int, Bool, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

Jacobi-Davidson for the `k` eigenvalues of a symmetric operator closest
to `target` (interior eigenvalues included).

The search space is expanded with the solution `t` of the projected
correction equation `(I - Q Q^T)(A - theta I)(I - Q Q^T) t = -r` (`Q`
holds the locked eigenvectors and the current Ritz vector), solved
approximately by GMRES; `precond`, if given, writes `K^{-1} r` for an
approximation `K` of `A - theta I` and is made consistent with the
projector. Harmonic Ritz extraction picks the Ritz vector with the
smallest `|A - target|` residual direction, which is reliable for
interior targets where ordinary Rayleigh-Ritz values do not converge to
the nearest eigenvalues. Converged vectors are locked and deflated.

# Errors
[`EigsError::Invalid`] for `k == 0` or `k > n`; [`EigsError::Dense`] if a
projected eigenproblem fails.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_jd_two_sided` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Float, Float, Int, Int, Int, Int, Bool, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

Two-sided Jacobi-Davidson for the `k` eigenvalues of a general real
operator nearest to the (complex) `target`, with **left and right**
eigenvectors.

Two search spaces `V` (right) and `W` (left), each orthonormal, are
expanded together. The projected pencil `(W^H (A - tau) V, W^H V)` gives
Petrov-Galerkin pairs: the Ritz value `theta`, the right Ritz vector
`u = V y` with residual `r = (A - tau - theta) u` orthogonal to `W`, and the
left Ritz vector `w = W z` with residual `s = (A - tau - theta)^H w`
orthogonal to `V`; the left vectors of the small pencil come from the
inverse of its right-eigenvector matrix, so the *two-sided Rayleigh
quotient* `theta = w^H A u / w^H u` is stationary (its error is quadratic in
the residuals, unlike the one-sided quotient for a non-normal `A`). The two
oblique correction equations
`(I - u w^H / w^H u)(A - theta)(I - u w^H / w^H u) t = -r` and the adjoint
one for `s` are solved by GMRES. Converged pairs are deflated *obliquely*:
locked right vectors `Q` and left vectors `P` (scaled so that
`p_j^H q_j = 1`, mutually biorthogonal for distinct eigenvalues) define the
projector `I - Q (P^H Q)^{-1} P^H` that keeps both spaces away from them.

`apply` is `x -> A x`, `apply_t` is `x -> A^T x` (the adjoint of the real
operator). A pair is accepted when both residuals are below
`opts.tol * max(|lambda|, 1)`. The standard (not harmonic) extraction is
used, so `target` should lie near the wanted eigenvalues.

# Errors
[`EigsError::Invalid`] for `k == 0` or `k > n`; [`EigsError::Dense`] if a
projected problem fails.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_eigs_krylov_schur` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, String, Float, Int, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native eigensolver over a checked operator matrix, retaining explicit entry reference scales. Eigenvectors are normalized native rays; eigenvalue and residual references are returned separately (generalized eigenvalues use A/B). Native algorithm identity, convergence reports and work limits are preserved.

Krylov-Schur eigensolver for a general real operator: the `k` eigenpairs
selected by `which`.

The Arnoldi factorisation `A V = V B + beta v e^T` of dimension `m`
(`opts.ncv`, default `max(2k + 1, 20)`) is contracted by computing the
Schur form of `B`, moving the wanted eigenvalues to the leading block and
truncating; the factorisation is then extended again. Ritz residuals come
from the last row of the Schur vectors and are exact for the Arnoldi
relation. Conjugate pairs are kept together.

# Errors
[`EigsError::Invalid`] for `k == 0` or `k > n`; [`EigsError::Dense`] if
the Schur iteration fails.

symmetric operator, using blocks of `block` vectors.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_geometric_solve` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/geometric-mg/v1, rssn/native/array/v1, None | Some(Tensor<1, Float>), String, String, Int, Int, Float, Int) -> rssn/native/multigrid-result/v1
```

Solves `A u = f` by repeated cycles from `u = 0` (or `x0`).

The history records `||f - A u||₂ / ||f||₂` for nonzero `f`.
For an exactly zero right-hand side, the denominator is
[`f64::MIN_POSITIVE`]. A nonzero relative residual that underflows
is reported as the smallest positive subnormal. Non-finite
right-hand sides or applied iterates give an undefined residual
(NaN). Only a finite residual at or below the tolerance converges.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_hooi` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Tensor<1, Int>, Int, Float) -> rssn/native/tucker/v1
```

Native tensor decomposition with explicit reference scale and bounded factor/order/sweep storage. Factors are normalized; reconstructed tensors retain the input physical domain.

Refine a truncated HOSVD using higher-order orthogonal iteration.

Each coordinate step computes the leading singular subspace after
projecting all other modes. Ranks are upper bounds and may be clamped to
the available subspace. Initialization is deterministic HOSVD; HOOI can
converge to a local optimum or stationary point. Inspect `relative_error`
independently from `converged`. Exhausting the sweep budget returns the
best observed approximation with `converged = false`. Residuals near
floating-point roundoff also terminate the iteration.

Input normalization protects intermediate norm calculations at uniformly
small/large scales. No Gram matrices or condition-number squaring are used.
Zero tensors use a rank-one zero core.

# Errors
Non-finite data, empty modes, invalid
ranks/tolerance/budget, SVD failure, or arithmetic overflow return an error.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_hosvd` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Tensor<1, Int>) -> rssn/native/hosvd/v1
```

Native tensor decomposition with explicit reference scale and bounded factor/order/sweep storage. Factors are normalized; reconstructed tensors retain the input physical domain.

The higher-order SVD (Tucker decomposition) of a dense tensor.

For each mode the tensor is unfolded to `n_k x prod(rest)`, the leading left
singular vectors of the unfolding become the factor, and the core is the
tensor contracted with every factor. `ranks` may be `None` for the numerical
multilinear rank of the unfoldings (at most `min(n_k, prod(rest))`, and less
when an unfolding is rank deficient in floating point); a requested rank
above that is clamped to it. The decomposition is exact before truncation
and gives `||T - C x U||_F <= sqrt(sum_k sum_{j > r_k} sigma_{k,j}^2)`.

# Errors
Fails when `ranks` does not have one entry per mode, when a requested rank
is zero, when a mode is empty, or when a mode unfolding has no nonzero
singular value.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_integrate_simplex` (Experimental)

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Native adaptive simplex integration of a retained compiled scalar field, with explicit independent coordinate and ordinate references. Each vertex is normalized by the coordinate reference; value/error dimensions are ordinate times coordinate^dimension. Native evaluation and dimension limits are preserved with a checked finite callback/work budget.

Integrate `f` over the simplex defined by `n + 1` vertices in `R^n`.

Dimensions 1 through 20 are accepted, although the underlying rule is
practical only in much lower dimensions. The result uses unsigned volume,
regardless of vertex orientation. A zero-volume simplex returns zero
without evaluating `f`. At least one tolerance must be positive.

The returned [`Integral::converged`] is false if the evaluation budget is
exhausted. If the budget cannot cover the initial grid, its value and error
are NaN and its evaluation count is zero, as in [`cubature_genz_malik`].
Error estimates are heuristic and cannot certify accuracy.

# Errors
Returns [`SimplexError::InvalidInput`] for malformed vertices or tolerances,
and reports non-finite integrands and arithmetic overflow separately.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_integrate_simplex_map` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/simplex-map/v1, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>, Float, Float, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Integrates a retained compiled scalar field over a prepared simplex using adaptive cubature. Geometry is reused. Give a positive value reference and normalized tolerances. Value and error have field dimension times coordinate dimension raised to the spatial rank.

Integrates a scalar function with the prepared geometry.

Uses the same tolerances and work budget as [`integrate_simplex`].

# Errors
Returns an error for invalid tolerances, a non-finite integrand or
a numerical overflow.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_lagrange_interpolation` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }) -> rssn/native/polynomial/v1
```

Native normalized-only convenience API: coordinates and ordinates are strictly dimensionless. Corresponding physical adapters accept explicit independent coordinate and ordinate references. Point/order/allocation bounds are enforced.

Constructs a Lagrange interpolating polynomial that passes through a given set of points.

Lagrange interpolation is a method of finding a polynomial that takes on certain values
at specified points. The resulting polynomial is unique and passes exactly through all given points.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a `Polynomial` struct representing the interpolating polynomial.

# Errors
Returns an error for repeated coordinates, nonfinite samples, or overflowing
divided differences or power-basis coefficients. Empty input returns zero.
For nonempty input the polynomial retains one coefficient per sample.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::lagrange_interpolation;

let points = vec![(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 4.0)];

let poly = lagrange_interpolation(&points).unwrap();

assert!((poly.eval(1.5) - 2.25).abs() < 1e-9);
```


Constructs a Lagrange interpolating polynomial that passes through a given set of points.

Lagrange interpolation is a method of finding a polynomial that takes on certain values
at specified points. The resulting polynomial is unique and passes exactly through all given points.

# Arguments

# Returns

# Errors

# Example

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_linear_interpolation` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/interpolation-curve/v1
```

Native interpolation over normalized samples with explicit coordinate and ordinate references. Physical queries and outputs are checked against retained domains; point/order/allocation bounds are enforced.

Piecewise-linear interpolation through `(x, y)`.

Second order in the node spacing for a smooth function: the error on a segment of
length `h` is `f''(xi) h^2 / 8`. Values outside the node range are extrapolated with
the first or the last segment.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples with strictly increasing `x`.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a closure `Arc<dyn Fn(f64) -> f64>` evaluating the interpolant.

# Errors
Returns an error if fewer than two points are given or the abscissae are not strictly
increasing.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::linear_interpolation;

let f = linear_interpolation(&[(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 4.0)]).unwrap();

assert!((f(0.5) - 0.5).abs() < 1e-12);

assert!((f(1.5) - 2.5).abs() < 1e-12);
```

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_lobpcg` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Float, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Actual native low-rank/operator method. Matrices and state arrays retain explicit physical references; orthonormal factors are dimensionless. Shapes, iterations, callbacks and allocations are bounded.

The `k` smallest eigenpairs of a symmetric operator of size `n` by LOBPCG.

`apply(x, y)` writes `A x`. `precondition`, when given, writes an
approximation of `A^-1 r` (it must be symmetric positive definite; the
identity is used otherwise). Each iteration performs a Rayleigh-Ritz
projection on the span of the current vectors, the preconditioned
residuals and the previous search directions, with the basis
re-orthonormalised every time, which is what keeps the method stable when
the directions become nearly dependent close to convergence.

# Errors
[`LowRankError::Shape`] when `k` is zero or more than `n / 3` would allow
(`3 k <= n` is needed for the trial subspace), or a product is not
finite, or when the tolerance is not positive and finite.
Returns [`LowRankError::NoConvergence`] when `max_iterations` pass with a
residual above `tol * max(1, |lambda|)`.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_minpoly_wiedemann` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/sparse-prime/v1, Int, Int) -> None | Some(Tensor<1, Int>)
```

Native exact sparse/domain operation specialized to BigRational or a validated prime field. Coefficients are normalized dimensionless exact values; finite shape, coefficient-bit and work budgets are enforced.

The minimal polynomial of a square matrix over `GF(p)` by Wiedemann's
algorithm, monic, lowest degree first.

The algorithm flattens `matrix` once into a Montgomery-domain CSR
workspace, multiplies by the matrix `2n` times per trial with delayed
`u128` row accumulation, and leases Krylov vectors from
[`crate::kernels::reuse::global_pool`]: no entry of the matrix is ever
changed, so there is no fill-in. One random projection yields a divisor
of the minimal polynomial, and the right one with probability at least
`1 - 2n/p`; the result here is the least common multiple over `trials`
projections (seeded, so the function is deterministic). `None` when the
matrix is not square.

```aevia

```

Native numerical method. Normalized coordinates and positive physical reference scales are checked; native object kind/session/lifetime and allocation/work budgets are enforced.

Computes the outer product of two tensors.

The outer product of two tensors `A` (rank `r`) and `B` (rank `s`)
results in a new tensor `C` of rank `r + s`. Each component of `C`
is the product of a component from `A` and a component from `B`.

# Arguments
* `a` - The first tensor (`ndarray::ArrayD<f64>`).
* `b` - The second tensor (`ndarray::ArrayD<f64>`).

# Returns
The resulting outer product tensor as an `ndarray::ArrayD<f64>`.

# Errors

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_pchip_interpolation` (Experimental)

```aevia
({ item0: Tensor<1, Float>, item1: Tensor<1, Float> }, Dyn<term>, Dyn<term>) -> rssn/native/interpolation-curve/v1
```

Native interpolation over normalized samples with explicit coordinate and ordinate references. Physical queries and outputs are checked against retained domains; point/order/allocation bounds are enforced.

Monotone piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation (PCHIP, Fritsch-Carlson).

The interpolant is `C^1` and, unlike a plain cubic spline, preserves the shape of the
data: on every interval its values stay inside the range of the two end ordinates, so
monotone data stay monotone and a step is not overshot. Third order in the node
spacing where the slope has one sign, second order at a data extremum, where the
slope estimate is clipped to zero — the price of shape preservation. Values outside
the node range are extrapolated with the first or the last Hermite cubic.

# Arguments
* `points` - A slice of `(x, y)` tuples with strictly increasing `x`.

# Returns
A `Result` containing a closure `Arc<dyn Fn(f64) -> f64>` evaluating the interpolant.

# Errors
Returns an error if fewer than two points are given or the abscissae are not strictly
increasing.

# Example
```rust
use rssn::kernels::interpolate::pchip_interpolation;

// A step: the monotone interpolant stays within [0, 1].
let step = [(0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0), (2.0, 1.0), (3.0, 1.0)];

let f = pchip_interpolation(&step).unwrap();

for k in 0..=30 {
    let v = f(f64::from(k) / 10.0);

    assert!((-1e-12..=1.0 + 1e-12).contains(&v));
}
```

```aevia
(Tensor<2, Float>, Int) -> Tensor<1, Tensor<2, Float>>
```

Checked native linear calculation in normalized reference coordinates. Physical tensors must be explicitly nondimensionalized; normalized outputs use the same declared reference basis.

The `phi_k(A)` functions, `k = 0..=p`, from one augmented matrix exponential.

The functions `phi_0(A), ..., phi_p(A)` where
`phi_0(z) = e^z` and `phi_k(z) = (phi_{k-1}(z) - 1/(k-1)!) / z`
(so `phi_1(z) = (e^z - 1)/z`), from one matrix exponential of the
augmented matrix `[[A, I, 0, ..], [0, 0, I, ..], ..]` (Sidje).

# Errors
As [`expm`].

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_pivoted_qr` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1) -> rssn/native/pivoted-qr/v1
```

Actual native low-rank/operator method. Matrices and state arrays retain explicit physical references; orthonormal factors are dimensionless. Shapes, iterations, callbacks and allocations are bounded.

Column-pivoted Householder QR (Businger and Golub).

At each step the remaining column of largest norm is brought forward, so
the diagonal of `R` decreases in magnitude and its decay reveals the
numerical rank. Column norms are downdated and recomputed when
cancellation makes the downdate unreliable. Each reflector applies to
contiguous columns, with large independent column batches running in parallel.

# Errors
[`LowRankError::Shape`] for inconsistent storage or non-finite entries,
and [`LowRankError::NoConvergence`] if the resulting factor exceeds the
representable floating-point range.

`tol * |R[0][0]|`. `None` picks `max(m, n) * eps`.

## `numerical_matrix.num_linear_randomized_svd` (Experimental)

```aevia
(rssn/native/array/v1, Int, Int, Int, Int) -> Dyn<term>
```

Approximates the leading singular triplets of a finite matrix with a seeded Gaussian sketch. Oversampling widens the sketch and power iterations improve separation of nearby singular values. The columns of u and v are dimensionless. Multiply each entry of s by singular_value_reference to obtain a singular value in the matrix's physical units.

A rank-`k` approximate singular value decomposition of an `m x n`
operator given by its products: `matvec(x, y)` writes `A x` (`x` of
length `n`, `y` of length `m`) and `rmatvec(y, x)` writes `A^T y`.

The range of `A` is sampled with `k + oversample` random vectors,
sharpened by power iterations with re-orthogonalisation between them, and
the small projected matrix is decomposed densely. The cost is
at most `2 (power_iterations + 1) (k + oversample)` products. Extreme
sampled columns are rescaled before orthogonalisation. Singular values
retain the scale of the original operator.

# Errors
[`LowRankError::Shape`] when `k` is zero or exceeds `min(m, n)`, or a
product returns non-finite numbers; [`LowRankError::NoConvergence`] when
the dense decomposition of the projected matrix fails.
